display_title: [XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

Restrict `IsEligibleScan` to skip scans where `AssociativeScanRewriter` combined with native `kLoop` or `kInput` fusions is faster:

1. Require `scan_dim_size > 1` so degenerate single-element scans do not launch a Triton kernel.
2. Require the scan dimension to be the most minor physical dimension of the input layout for coalesced memory accesses.
3. Skip small scans (`scan_dim_size <= 1024`) without a `kCustom` fusion producer when their non-scalar producer or consumer neighborhood reaches a data-movement or indexing op that Triton cannot fuse (`slice`, `pad`, `concatenate`, `gather`, `scatter`, `reverse`, `dynamic-slice`, `dynamic-update-slice`), avoiding splitting a single native fusion around a Triton scan kernel.

With default flags, this change has no effect.

display_title: Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

head_commit.message:
Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

With `prefer_estimated_configs`, each instruction's estimated configs were
compiled serially on the calling thread.

Now we split the config assignment into 3 stages:
* Look up forced or cached config
* If applicable, get an estimated config <- now they are compiled in parallel
* Get a tuned (if autotuning) or a first compilable/default config (if not)

This is similar to what we've been doing already, just split into stages more explicitly. We need to trigger the tuned and fallback config getter from the main thread, since getting supported configs is not thread-safe.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Switch One-Shot Triton AllGather to push-based scratch writes.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Switch One-Shot Triton AllGather to push-based scratch writes.

  * Scratch buffer is now sized based on output instead of input.
  * Instead of each rank pulling subtiles from peer input buffers over NVLink now
    we push the entire tile to peer scratch.
  * This improves 16 device AllGather latency by 1.22x-1.54x across 1 KiB-32 MiB
  * Raises `kMaxAllGatherSizeBytes` from 16 MiB to 32 MiB and
    `kAllGatherMaxBlocksPerGrid` from 64 to 128.

head_commit.message:
Add `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` to query the Linux dma-buf
location (`{fd, offset, size}`) of an on-device buffer for external
access.

The query returns the raw buffer's location within the underlying
dma-buf, with `offset` measured from the dma-buf start. The location
remains valid as long as the caller holds a reference to the raw
buffer, while ordering external access against device execution
remains the caller's responsibility. Unsupported backends and plugins
built against earlier API versions return `Unimplemented`.

display_title: PR #50683: [XLA:GPU] Set max_total_seq_len for packed cuDNN flash attention backward

head_commit.message:
PR #50683: [XLA:GPU] Set max_total_seq_len for packed cuDNN flash attention backward

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50683

📝 Summary of Changes

`GetCudnnFlashAttentionBackwardOperationGraph` now tells cuDNN the maximum packed token count for packed (ragged) SDPA backward. When `max_seg_per_batch` > 1, it computes `max_total_seq_len_q = B * S_q` and `max_total_seq_len_kv = B * S_kv`. It passes them to the graph via `set_max_total_seq_len_q` and `set_max_total_seq_len_kv`. Dense and padding-only graphs are unchanged.

🎯 Justification

For packed graphs, Q/K/V/dO/O/dQ/dK/dV are declared as shape `[B, H, S, D]` with additional attribute `max_seg_per_batch` in XLA to indicate how many segments are packed inside each batch. Without this setting, cuDNN sizes the backward workspace for `B * max_seg_per_batch * S` tokens. The real token count cannot exceed `B * S`, because each of the B physical rows holds at most S tokens. The two dominant workspace terms, `softmax_sum` and the FP32 `dQ_accum`, scale with this token count and shrink by a factor of `max_seg_per_batch`.

Workloads that benefit: packed or segmented-sequence attention training, such as JAX/Flax/MaxText with `max_segments_per_batch` > 1, where backward workspace is often the peak-memory driver.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

🧪 Unit Tests:

cudnn_flash_attention_test.cc

display_title: Fix clang-tidy target selection for CUDA sources

head_commit.message:
Fix clang-tidy target selection for CUDA sources

`@bazel_clang_tidy` always appends `-xc++` and forwards target `copts` directly to `clang-tidy`, so running it on `.cu.cc` files or `cuda_library` targets fails on CUDA device syntax and NVCC-only flags (such as `-Xcuda-fatbinary` and `-nvcc_options`).

So this change excludes `.cu.cc` and `.cu.h` files from `CHANGED_FILES` in `build_tools/ci/run_clang_tidy.sh` (letting CUDA-only changes exit before starting Bazel) and filters `cuda_library` and `.cu` targets out of the `cquery` target list when a shared header or `.cc` file changes.

display_title: PR #51174: [XLA:GPU] Enable automatic scheduler memory fencing by default

head_commit.message:
PR #51174: [XLA:GPU] Enable automatic scheduler memory fencing by default

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51174

📝 Summary of Changes

Enable GPU scheduler memory fencing by default with `--xla_gpu_experimental_scheduler_memory_fencing_threshold_bytes=0`. Retain the existing `--xla_gpu_experimental_scheduler_memory_fencing_slack_windows=1` default and update the default-options regression test to assert both values.

- **Threshold bytes:** negative values disable fencing; `0` automatically selects 1% of the scheduler memory limit; positive values select an explicit minimum buffer size, capped at that limit. Before latency-hiding scheduling, the pass adds control dependencies to constrain how long users of large buffers can be deferred, limiting live-range inflation.
- **Slack windows:** how many async-operation windows those users may be deferred beyond the buffer’s last-use window in the reference schedule. `1` permits one window of flexibility; larger values allow more reordering and potentially higher peak memory. Users can opt out with threshold `-1`.

🎯 Justification

The proposed defaults reduce peak allocator memory for Gemma2-9B (6.779%), Qwen3-30B-A3B (3.129%), and GPT-OSS-20B (1.510%) in the shard-autotuning-enabled campaign. The reduced DeepSeek-V3 configurations also show 0.787–3.248% lower iteration latency. Benefits are workload-dependent: the table includes latency regressions, memory increases, and failures; it does not establish a universal speedup or lower physical VRAM requirements.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark

**BASE = threshold −1 / slack 1; 0/1 = threshold 0 / slack 1. Improvement = 100 × (BASE − 0/1) / BASE; positive means faster or less memory.** Percentages use unrounded measurements.

| Workload                        | Valid runs BASE / 0/1 | BASE latency (ms) | 0/1 latency (ms) | Latency improvement | BASE peak (GiB/GPU) | 0/1 peak (GiB/GPU) | Memory improvement |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------: | ----------------: | ---------------: | ------------------: | ------------------: | -----------------: | -----------------: |
| deepseek2-16b (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          2492.670 |         2485.517 |             +0.287% |             121.795 |            123.009 |            -0.997% |
| gemma2-9b-fp8 (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          2400.005 |         2398.480 |             +0.064% |             115.650 |            107.810 |            +6.779% |
| llama3.1-8b-fp16 (shard=on)     |                   2/2 |          2654.079 |         2601.087 |             +1.997% |             141.231 |            141.231 |             0.000% |
| qwen3-8b-fp8 (shard=on)         |                   2/2 |          2140.149 |         2161.023 |             -0.975% |             113.395 |            113.395 |             0.000% |
| gpt-oss-20b (shard=on)          |                   2/2 |          4931.738 |         4940.903 |             -0.186% |             134.947 |            132.909 |            +1.510% |
| qwen3-32b-fp8 (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          2521.475 |         2524.145 |             -0.106% |             104.467 |            104.467 |             0.000% |
| llama3.3-70b-fp8 (shard=on)     |                   2/2 |          5834.719 |         5836.766 |             -0.035% |              95.821 |             95.821 |             0.000% |
| qwen3-30b-a3b (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          4357.009 |         4381.382 |             -0.559% |              77.342 |             74.922 |            +3.129% |
| DeepSeek-V3 GA2 (17 layers) [a] |                   1/1 |          3569.576 |         3541.478 |             +0.787% |             135.638 |            135.692 |            -0.039% |
| deepseek2-236b (shard=on)       |                   0/0 |               OOM |              OOM |                   — |                   — |                  — |                  — |
| llama4-17b-16e (shard=on)       |                   2/2 |         13265.645 |        13315.224 |             -0.374% |             143.705 |            143.705 |             0.000% |
| DeepSeek-V3 GA2 (17 layers) [b] |                   1/1 |          4621.304 |         4471.194 |             +3.248% |             111.273 |            109.924 |            +1.212% |
| DeepSeek-V3 GA2 (17 layers) [c] |                   3/3 |          4720.861 |         4675.966 |             +0.951% |              96.747 |             94.039 |            +2.800% |

- `shard=on` identifies `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=true` in both comparison arms. These campaigns use GB200, command buffers off, PGLE off, and pinned `maxtext-2026-10-18`.
- DeepSeek-V3 [a]/[b]/[c] identify the 8-node / 16-node / 32-node configurations. All use GB200, the **reduced 17-layer GA=2 reproducer**, command buffers and automatic PGLE, and `maxtext-2026-10-15`. [a]/[b] use the original single BASE/0/1 pair; [c] uses three runs per arm. The repeated slack-2/slack-0 winners at 8/16 nodes are not substituted for the requested slack-1 setting.
- Latency is mean synchronized full training-iteration latency over steps 40–60, using the slowest rank each step; startup/compilation are excluded. Peak memory is the full-process JAX allocator high-water, maximum across ranks/devices, averaged over the included runs. It is not reserved or sampled physical GPU memory. Compare within each row; configurations and software differ across studies.
- `llama3.1-8b-fp16` is the catalog name, but the tested recipe uses FP8. Its apparent ~2% latency improvement has overlapping repeat ranges. Small differences have limited repeat coverage. DeepSeek-V3 is not the full 61-layer/671B model.
- OOM arms have no valid percentage. DeepSeek2-236B failed with application OOM on all ranks under both settings. Diagnostics and setup failures are excluded. The table contains 13 configuration rows and 12 valid numerical comparisons.

🧪 Unit Tests

Updated `//xla:debug_options_flags_test` to assert automatic threshold `0` and slack `1`. `git show --check` passed. The focused Bazel test was **not run**: remote source transfer timed out before test submission. No compilation was run locally.

🧪 Execution Tests

The recorded workloads completed 65 iterations per rank for successful trials, with successful process exits, finite losses, flags and software provenance audited. These are existing explicit-flag benchmark results, not a new run of this default-changing commit; finite losses do not prove convergence equivalence. No additional GPU execution test or public-HLO microbenchmark was run for this two-file default change.

name: CI
display_title: Fix base branch fetch in clang-format workflow

head_commit.message:
Fix base branch fetch in clang-format workflow

In `.github/workflows/clang_format.yml`, `git fetch origin main --depth=1` truncates `origin/main` to a single commit, so `git merge-base` in `build_tools/ci/run_clang_format.sh` fails as soon as `main` advances past a PR's base commit. Hardcoding `main` also breaks PRs that target release branches.

So this change switches checkout to `fetch-depth: '100'` (avoiding downloading all branches and tags) and fetches the full history of `${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-main}`, matching `.github/workflows/clang_tidy.yml`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Disable NCCL RMA kernels for non-RMA buffers.
With NCCL 2.32 XLA can disable NCCL RMA kernels and copy engine usage when buffers are not allocated in the symmetric memory space (or are remotely accessible). This is useful for a situation when module is getting executed while another module has cached NCCL window.

This also allows us to register NCCL window bigger then collective memory space, because now we can disable symmetric NCCL collectives at the default memory space manually.

name: CI
display_title: Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

head_commit.message:
Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

With `prefer_estimated_configs`, each instruction's estimated configs were
compiled serially on the calling thread.

Now we split the config assignment into 3 stages:
* Look up forced or cached config
* If applicable, get an estimated config <- now they are compiled in parallel
* Get a tuned (if autotuning) or a first compilable/default config (if not)

This is similar to what we've been doing already, just split into stages more explicitly. We need to trigger the tuned and fallback config getter from the main thread, since getting supported configs is not thread-safe.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 988186995

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Preserve shared `inlineable="xla_late"` callees in FlattenCallGraph.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve shared `inlineable="xla_late"` callees in FlattenCallGraph.

* Add `flatten_non_inlineable_calls` option (default `false`) to `FlattenCallGraph`.
* Constrain the single-argument `bool` constructor with `std::enable_if_t<std::is_same_v<T, bool>>` so passing a function pointer (e.g. `AddPass<FlattenCallGraph>(FlattenCallGraph::SkipCloningForCalls)` in compiler pass pipelines) binds to the `absl::AnyInvocable` overload instead of implicitly converting the non-null function pointer to `true` via C++ standard boolean conversion.
* When `flatten_non_inlineable_calls=false`, skip cloning callees at `kCall` sites annotated with `frontend_attributes={inlineable="xla_late"}` so deduplicated computations remain shared across late-inlined call sites until explicit late flattening (`FlattenCallGraph(/*flatten_non_inlineable_calls=*/true)`).
* Handle mixed callers (where both standard calls or while/conditional bodies and `xla_late` calls target the same computation)

display_title: PR #51174: [XLA:GPU] Enable automatic scheduler memory fencing by default

head_commit.message:
PR #51174: [XLA:GPU] Enable automatic scheduler memory fencing by default

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51174

📝 Summary of Changes

Enable GPU scheduler memory fencing by default with `--xla_gpu_experimental_scheduler_memory_fencing_threshold_bytes=0`. Retain the existing `--xla_gpu_experimental_scheduler_memory_fencing_slack_windows=1` default and update the default-options regression test to assert both values.

- **Threshold bytes:** negative values disable fencing; `0` automatically selects 1% of the scheduler memory limit; positive values select an explicit minimum buffer size, capped at that limit. Before latency-hiding scheduling, the pass adds control dependencies to constrain how long users of large buffers can be deferred, limiting live-range inflation.
- **Slack windows:** how many async-operation windows those users may be deferred beyond the buffer’s last-use window in the reference schedule. `1` permits one window of flexibility; larger values allow more reordering and potentially higher peak memory. Users can opt out with threshold `-1`.

🎯 Justification

The proposed defaults reduce peak allocator memory for Gemma2-9B (6.779%), Qwen3-30B-A3B (3.129%), and GPT-OSS-20B (1.510%) in the shard-autotuning-enabled campaign. The reduced DeepSeek-V3 configurations also show 0.787–3.248% lower iteration latency. Benefits are workload-dependent: the table includes latency regressions, memory increases, and failures; it does not establish a universal speedup or lower physical VRAM requirements.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark

**BASE = threshold −1 / slack 1; 0/1 = threshold 0 / slack 1. Improvement = 100 × (BASE − 0/1) / BASE; positive means faster or less memory.** Percentages use unrounded measurements.

| Workload                        | Valid runs BASE / 0/1 | BASE latency (ms) | 0/1 latency (ms) | Latency improvement | BASE peak (GiB/GPU) | 0/1 peak (GiB/GPU) | Memory improvement |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------: | ----------------: | ---------------: | ------------------: | ------------------: | -----------------: | -----------------: |
| deepseek2-16b (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          2492.670 |         2485.517 |             +0.287% |             121.795 |            123.009 |            -0.997% |
| gemma2-9b-fp8 (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          2400.005 |         2398.480 |             +0.064% |             115.650 |            107.810 |            +6.779% |
| llama3.1-8b-fp16 (shard=on)     |                   2/2 |          2654.079 |         2601.087 |             +1.997% |             141.231 |            141.231 |             0.000% |
| qwen3-8b-fp8 (shard=on)         |                   2/2 |          2140.149 |         2161.023 |             -0.975% |             113.395 |            113.395 |             0.000% |
| gpt-oss-20b (shard=on)          |                   2/2 |          4931.738 |         4940.903 |             -0.186% |             134.947 |            132.909 |            +1.510% |
| qwen3-32b-fp8 (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          2521.475 |         2524.145 |             -0.106% |             104.467 |            104.467 |             0.000% |
| llama3.3-70b-fp8 (shard=on)     |                   2/2 |          5834.719 |         5836.766 |             -0.035% |              95.821 |             95.821 |             0.000% |
| qwen3-30b-a3b (shard=on)        |                   2/2 |          4357.009 |         4381.382 |             -0.559% |              77.342 |             74.922 |            +3.129% |
| DeepSeek-V3 GA2 (17 layers) [a] |                   1/1 |          3569.576 |         3541.478 |             +0.787% |             135.638 |            135.692 |            -0.039% |
| deepseek2-236b (shard=on)       |                   0/0 |               OOM |              OOM |                   — |                   — |                  — |                  — |
| llama4-17b-16e (shard=on)       |                   2/2 |         13265.645 |        13315.224 |             -0.374% |             143.705 |            143.705 |             0.000% |
| DeepSeek-V3 GA2 (17 layers) [b] |                   1/1 |          4621.304 |         4471.194 |             +3.248% |             111.273 |            109.924 |            +1.212% |
| DeepSeek-V3 GA2 (17 layers) [c] |                   3/3 |          4720.861 |         4675.966 |             +0.951% |              96.747 |             94.039 |            +2.800% |

- `shard=on` identifies `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=true` in both comparison arms. These campaigns use GB200, command buffers off, PGLE off, and pinned `maxtext-2026-10-18`.
- DeepSeek-V3 [a]/[b]/[c] identify the 8-node / 16-node / 32-node configurations. All use GB200, the **reduced 17-layer GA=2 reproducer**, command buffers and automatic PGLE, and `maxtext-2026-10-15`. [a]/[b] use the original single BASE/0/1 pair; [c] uses three runs per arm. The repeated slack-2/slack-0 winners at 8/16 nodes are not substituted for the requested slack-1 setting.
- Latency is mean synchronized full training-iteration latency over steps 40–60, using the slowest rank each step; startup/compilation are excluded. Peak memory is the full-process JAX allocator high-water, maximum across ranks/devices, averaged over the included runs. It is not reserved or sampled physical GPU memory. Compare within each row; configurations and software differ across studies.
- `llama3.1-8b-fp16` is the catalog name, but the tested recipe uses FP8. Its apparent ~2% latency improvement has overlapping repeat ranges. Small differences have limited repeat coverage. DeepSeek-V3 is not the full 61-layer/671B model.
- OOM arms have no valid percentage. DeepSeek2-236B failed with application OOM on all ranks under both settings. Diagnostics and setup failures are excluded. The table contains 13 configuration rows and 12 valid numerical comparisons.

🧪 Unit Tests

Updated `//xla:debug_options_flags_test` to assert automatic threshold `0` and slack `1`. `git show --check` passed. The focused Bazel test was **not run**: remote source transfer timed out before test submission. No compilation was run locally.

🧪 Execution Tests

The recorded workloads completed 65 iterations per rank for successful trials, with successful process exits, finite losses, flags and software provenance audited. These are existing explicit-flag benchmark results, not a new run of this default-changing commit; finite losses do not prove convergence equivalence. No additional GPU execution test or public-HLO microbenchmark was run for this two-file default change.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

Restrict `ScanRewriterTriton::IsEligibleScan` to skip scans where `AssociativeScanRewriter` combined with native `kLoop` or `kInput` fusions produces fewer kernel launches or better memory coalescing:

1. Require `scan_dim_size > 1` so degenerate single-element scans are left to `AssociativeScanRewriter` instead of launching a Triton kernel.
2. Require the scan dimension to be the most minor physical dimension of the input layout (`LayoutUtil::Minor(input_shape.layout(), 0) == scan_dim`) when a layout is present, ensuring coalesced memory accesses along the scan dimension.
3. Reject small scans (`scan_dim_size <= 1024`) without a `kCustom` fusion producer when their bounded non-effective-scalar producer or consumer neighborhood (walking through elementwise ops, `kBroadcast`, `kBitcast`, and `kReshape`) touches a loop or input data-movement or indexing op (`kConcatenate`, `kDynamicSlice`, `kDynamicUpdateSlice`, `kGather`, `kPad`, `kReverse`, `kScatter`, `kSlice`). For scans up to 3 radix-16 reduction levels, keeping the lowered scan in the surrounding native fusion avoids splitting the fusion around a standalone Triton scan kernel.

With default flags, this change has no effect.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Enable `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` by default.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Enable `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` by default.

Enabling `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` by default lowers eligible associative `HloOpcode::kScan` ops (`cumsum`, `cumprod`, `cummin`, `cummax`) on GPU to Triton fusions (`__triton`) via `ScanRewriterTriton`.

Across the 35-cell `f32[B, N]` scan benchmark sweep (`B` in `{1, 4, 16, 64, 256}`, `N` in `{1024, 4096, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144}`), the Triton scan emitter achieves 1.45x–3.20x speedups on A100, 1.16x–3.62x on H100, and 1.15x–4.35x on B200 with zero regressions, and fuses `softmax` + exclusive `cumsum` + mask (`K <= 128`) into a single Triton kernel (1.90x–2.19x speedup on H100 and B200).

display_title: Extract ResolveCudnnSupport and fail on uncompiled cuDNN ops

head_commit.message:
Extract ResolveCudnnSupport and fail on uncompiled cuDNN ops

Extract `ResolveCudnnSupport` into `xla/service/gpu/cudnn_support_utils.h` and lazily resolve `se::dnn::DnnSupport*` inside `CuDnnFusionCompiler` and `CuDnnCustomCallCompiler` only when a cuDNN fusion or custom call is actually encountered.

Before this change, compiling devicelessly without cuDNN deviceless compilation enabled would silently skip CuDnnFusionCompiler. Compilation succeeded, but the resulting executable failed at runtime when it tried to deserialize the cuDNN graph. With this change, we fail at compile time instead.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008072380

display_title: [XLA] Preserve shared `inlineable="xla_late"` callees in FlattenCallGraph.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve shared `inlineable="xla_late"` and `inlineable="false"` callees in FlattenCallGraph.

* Add `flatten_non_inlineable_calls` option (default `false`) to `FlattenCallGraph`.
* Constrain the single-argument `bool` constructor with `std::enable_if_t<std::is_same_v<T, bool>>` so passing a function pointer (e.g. `AddPass<FlattenCallGraph>(FlattenCallGraph::SkipCloningForCalls)` in compiler pass pipelines) binds to the `absl::AnyInvocable` overload instead of implicitly converting the non-null function pointer to `true` via C++ standard boolean conversion.
* When `flatten_non_inlineable_calls=false`, skip cloning callees at `kCall` sites annotated with `frontend_attributes={inlineable="xla_late"}` or `frontend_attributes={inlineable="false"}` so deduplicated computations remain shared across late-inlined call sites until explicit late flattening (`FlattenCallGraph(/*flatten_non_inlineable_calls=*/true)`).
* Handle mixed callers (where both standard calls or while/conditional bodies and `xla_late` calls target the same computation)

display_title: PR #50988: [XLA:GPU] Splat scalar operands in Triton atomics lowering

head_commit.message:
PR #50988: [XLA:GPU] Splat scalar operands in Triton atomics lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50988

#ai-generated

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50877.

## Summary of changes

Splat scalar `value` and `expected` operands to the pointer tensor shape before
creating `tt.extern_elementwise` in `LowerAtomicWriteOp` and
`LowerAtomicSpinWaitOp`. Scalar-pointer operations retain scalar operands.

Update the atomic-write and atomic-spin-wait FileCheck expectations, including
64-pointer masked cases that check the scalar splat and mask forwarding. Add a
full-pipeline regression test for a 64-rank block barrier, atomic write and
atomic spin-wait with `num-warps=1`, and remove the incorrect automatic-broadcast
comments.

## Justification

Small one-shot all-reduces over 64 devices can fail during Triton-to-LLVM
lowering with:

```text
size mismatch when packing elements for LLVM struct expected 2 but got 1
```

The block barrier passes a tensor of signal pointers and a scalar signal value
to the atomics lowering. With 64 ranks and one warp, each thread owns two
pointers, but the unsplatted scalar contributes only one value. Splatting the
value gives each pointer a corresponding operand without disabling the
collective kernel or changing its selection policy.

This was observed while compiling MaxText Llama 3.1 405B training on 64 GB200
GPUs. Thanks to @ksew1 for reporting the failure and identifying the block-barrier
atomics mechanism in #50877.

## Kind of contribution

Bug fix with regression coverage.

## Regression coverage

The atomics tests check both the scalar-to-tensor splat and the unchanged mask
operand. `triton_xla_atomics_pipeline.mlir` reaches LLVM through
`--triton-xla-pipeline='target=10.0 num-warps=1'`, covering the block barrier
and both unmasked atomic operations at 64 ranks.

Mask forwarding is checked at the atomics rewrite level. A separate existing
mask-type mismatch in the CUDA extern-atomics lowering prevents an `i1`-masked
case from completing the full pipeline.

## Execution tests

### Deviceless compiler reproducer

Save this as `repro.hlo`:

```hlo
HloModule repro, num_partitions=64

add {
  a = s32[] parameter(0)
  b = s32[] parameter(1)
  ROOT r = s32[] add(a, b)
}

ENTRY main {
  p = s32[] parameter(0)
  ROOT ar = s32[] all-reduce(p), channel_id=1,
    replica_groups=[1,64]<=[64], use_global_device_ids=true, to_apply=add
}
```

From the XLA repository root, using a CUDA-enabled `hlo-opt` build:

```bash
hlo-opt repro.hlo --platform=CUDA --stage=ptx \
  --xla_gpu_topology_filename=1x16x4 \
  --xla_gpu_target_config_filename=xla/backends/gpu/target_config/specs/gb200.txtpb
```

The topology and target configuration allow compilation without allocating
64 GPUs. Repeat with `--stage=hlo` to inspect `kernel_strategy` and confirm the
Triton one-shot path. The build must provide its required CUDA runtime libraries.

The following before/after comparison was run at
[XLA 9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5](https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5)
on aarch64 with CUDA 13.5, keeping the source revision and build configuration
fixed and changing only this patch:

| Case | Unpatched | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `num_partitions=64` | Original LLVM packing error; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `replica_count=64` | Same error | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 32 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `f32[256]`, 64 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, two warps | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, cross-host one-shot disabled | Compiles using the default strategy | Compiles using the default strategy |

For the 32-device control, change `num_partitions` to 32, use
`replica_groups=[1,32]<=[32]`, and select topology `1x8x4`. For the `f32[256]`
control, use `f32[256]` for the entry parameter and all-reduce result and `f32[]`
for the reduction computation's operands and result. The disabled-path control
adds `--xla_gpu_unsupported_use_cross_host_one_shot_kernel=`.

### Training validation

A JAX CUDA plugin/jaxlib build from the same source tree with the patch completed
30 training steps for both BF16 and NVFP4 Llama 3.1 405B on 16 hosts with 4 GB200
GPUs each, with FSDP=64, sequence length 4096, and batch size 2 per device.
Cross-host one-shot remained enabled by default; no collective-kernel workaround
was used. Neither run reproduced the compiler crash.

BF16 loss matched the earlier opt-out run within 0.002 at every step, with final
loss 11.658. NVFP4 default-path runs on the same patched build ended at 10.312
and 10.439; an opt-out run on that build ended at 10.354. The observed 0.127
difference between identical-config repeats exceeds the initial 0.048 gap
between the first patched run and the earlier unpatched opt-out run (10.264).
These repeats weaken the initial numerical-regression concern, but do not
establish numerical equivalence.

### Scope of the evidence

The runtime and deviceless PTX comparisons above apply to XLA
`9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5` on aarch64/GB200.

The implementation and new full-pipeline regression test were also built and
validated at `cf8a4e9ce78d390b127abb8be17084e1d6cbba63` on aarch64 Linux with
CUDA targeting `sm_100`. Adding only the pipeline test to unpatched main
reproduces the original LLVM packing error; adding the splat change makes it
pass.

This branch is rebased onto `dd678a263b79780a179e7a61863c8d0bdcc276d1`.
The implementation and full-pipeline test match the validated versions.
The additional 64-rank masked rewrite cases are new in this revision.
The 64-GPU training and PTX comparisons have not been repeated on this base.

head_commit.message:
Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

With `prefer_estimated_configs`, each instruction's estimated configs were
compiled serially on the calling thread.

Now we split the config assignment into 3 stages:
* Look up forced or cached config
* If applicable, get an estimated config <- now they are compiled in parallel
* Get a tuned (if autotuning) or a first compilable/default config (if not)

This is similar to what we've been doing already, just split into stages more explicitly. We need to trigger the tuned and fallback config getter from the main thread, since getting supported configs is not thread-safe.

display_title: Clean up xla::LayoutAssignment and switch to single pass propagation

head_commit.message:
Clean up xla::LayoutAssignment and switch to single pass propagation

## Problem

`xla::LayoutAssignment` previously ran up to two full constraint propagation
rounds, rebuilding dataflow state and clearing prior HLO layout mutations
between passes. That multiround structure duplicated state and relied on
fragile raw shape rewrites inside while loops during final layout assignment.

## Approach

Replace the multiround loop with a single pass pipeline built on
`HloDataflowPropagation`. Propagate mandatory and custom call constraints across
computation boundaries before assigning unconstrained defaults, then finalize
subcomputations and input output aliasing in postorder.

Converge while loop state layouts iteratively during subcomputation
finalization, and preserve memory spaces on automatic entry layouts. Track
enforcing instructions and priorities on buffer and operand constraints without
laundering nonmandatory hints. Pair variadic collective operands per element,
propagate reduced layouts through `kReduce`, clone nested shared conditional
branches deterministically, and forward layouts across `kAsyncUpdate`.

## Tests

- `//xla/service:layout_assignment_test`: pins single pass propagation across
  while loops, async chains, conditionals, collectives, reductions, priorities,
  and entry aliasing.
- `//xla/hlo/analysis:hlo_dataflow_analysis_test`: pins deterministic caller
  boundary ordering and while condition boundary guards.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1002777961

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Simplify and optimize CpuLayoutAssignment

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Simplify and optimize CpuLayoutAssignment

## Problem

`CpuLayoutAssignment` built temporary `Shape` and `std::vector` objects on
every operand to construct row major and column major layouts. Tuple shaped
`kAllGather` and `kReduceScatter` instructions also left operand layout
constraints unset, letting downstream users overwrite their mandatory major
dimension layouts.

## Approach

Replace `RowMajorShape` and `ColMajorShape` with `LayoutUtil` helpers that
clear preexisting layout fields and avoid heap allocations. Constrain both
tuple outputs and array operands on `kAllGather` and `kReduceScatter` before
assigning default layouts to remaining rank 2 or higher array operands. Skip
1D constants in `ShouldMakeOperandColumnMajor` because row major and column
major layouts are identical for rank at most 1 shapes.

Existing valid CPU programs keep the same assigned layouts. Tuple collectives
and inputs with preexisting tiles or split configs now receive clean host
layouts. No flags are added.

## Tests

- `//xla/service/cpu:cpu_layout_assignment_test` pins tile and split config
  stripping, 1D constant dots, and array and variadic `all-gather` and
  `reduce-scatter` layouts.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1002777875

display_title: PR #50988: [XLA:GPU] Splat scalar operands in Triton atomics lowering

head_commit.message:
PR #50988: [XLA:GPU] Splat scalar operands in Triton atomics lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50988

#ai-generated

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50877.

## Summary of changes

Splat scalar `value` and `expected` operands to the pointer tensor shape before
creating `tt.extern_elementwise` in `LowerAtomicWriteOp` and
`LowerAtomicSpinWaitOp`. Scalar-pointer operations retain scalar operands.

Update the atomic-write and atomic-spin-wait FileCheck expectations, including
64-pointer masked cases that check the scalar splat and mask forwarding. Add a
full-pipeline regression test for a 64-rank block barrier, atomic write and
atomic spin-wait with `num-warps=1`, and remove the incorrect automatic-broadcast
comments.

## Justification

Small one-shot all-reduces over 64 devices can fail during Triton-to-LLVM
lowering with:

```text
size mismatch when packing elements for LLVM struct expected 2 but got 1
```

The block barrier passes a tensor of signal pointers and a scalar signal value
to the atomics lowering. With 64 ranks and one warp, each thread owns two
pointers, but the unsplatted scalar contributes only one value. Splatting the
value gives each pointer a corresponding operand without disabling the
collective kernel or changing its selection policy.

This was observed while compiling MaxText Llama 3.1 405B training on 64 GB200
GPUs. Thanks to @ksew1 for reporting the failure and identifying the block-barrier
atomics mechanism in #50877.

## Kind of contribution

Bug fix with regression coverage.

## Regression coverage

The atomics tests check both the scalar-to-tensor splat and the unchanged mask
operand. `triton_xla_atomics_pipeline.mlir` reaches LLVM through
`--triton-xla-pipeline='target=10.0 num-warps=1'`, covering the block barrier
and both unmasked atomic operations at 64 ranks.

Mask forwarding is checked at the atomics rewrite level. A separate existing
mask-type mismatch in the CUDA extern-atomics lowering prevents an `i1`-masked
case from completing the full pipeline.

## Execution tests

### Deviceless compiler reproducer

Save this as `repro.hlo`:

```hlo
HloModule repro, num_partitions=64

add {
  a = s32[] parameter(0)
  b = s32[] parameter(1)
  ROOT r = s32[] add(a, b)
}

ENTRY main {
  p = s32[] parameter(0)
  ROOT ar = s32[] all-reduce(p), channel_id=1,
    replica_groups=[1,64]<=[64], use_global_device_ids=true, to_apply=add
}
```

From the XLA repository root, using a CUDA-enabled `hlo-opt` build:

```bash
hlo-opt repro.hlo --platform=CUDA --stage=ptx \
  --xla_gpu_topology_filename=1x16x4 \
  --xla_gpu_target_config_filename=xla/backends/gpu/target_config/specs/gb200.txtpb
```

The topology and target configuration allow compilation without allocating
64 GPUs. Repeat with `--stage=hlo` to inspect `kernel_strategy` and confirm the
Triton one-shot path. The build must provide its required CUDA runtime libraries.

The following before/after comparison was run at
[XLA 9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5](https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5)
on aarch64 with CUDA 13.5, keeping the source revision and build configuration
fixed and changing only this patch:

| Case | Unpatched | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `num_partitions=64` | Original LLVM packing error; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `replica_count=64` | Same error | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 32 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `f32[256]`, 64 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, two warps | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, cross-host one-shot disabled | Compiles using the default strategy | Compiles using the default strategy |

For the 32-device control, change `num_partitions` to 32, use
`replica_groups=[1,32]<=[32]`, and select topology `1x8x4`. For the `f32[256]`
control, use `f32[256]` for the entry parameter and all-reduce result and `f32[]`
for the reduction computation's operands and result. The disabled-path control
adds `--xla_gpu_unsupported_use_cross_host_one_shot_kernel=`.

### Training validation

A JAX CUDA plugin/jaxlib build from the same source tree with the patch completed
30 training steps for both BF16 and NVFP4 Llama 3.1 405B on 16 hosts with 4 GB200
GPUs each, with FSDP=64, sequence length 4096, and batch size 2 per device.
Cross-host one-shot remained enabled by default; no collective-kernel workaround
was used. Neither run reproduced the compiler crash.

BF16 loss matched the earlier opt-out run within 0.002 at every step, with final
loss 11.658. NVFP4 default-path runs on the same patched build ended at 10.312
and 10.439; an opt-out run on that build ended at 10.354. The observed 0.127
difference between identical-config repeats exceeds the initial 0.048 gap
between the first patched run and the earlier unpatched opt-out run (10.264).
These repeats weaken the initial numerical-regression concern, but do not
establish numerical equivalence.

### Scope of the evidence

The runtime and deviceless PTX comparisons above apply to XLA
`9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5` on aarch64/GB200.

The implementation and new full-pipeline regression test were also built and
validated at `cf8a4e9ce78d390b127abb8be17084e1d6cbba63` on aarch64 Linux with
CUDA targeting `sm_100`. Adding only the pipeline test to unpatched main
reproduces the original LLVM packing error; adding the splat change makes it
pass.

This branch is rebased onto `dd678a263b79780a179e7a61863c8d0bdcc276d1`.
The implementation and full-pipeline test match the validated versions.
The additional 64-rank masked rewrite cases are new in this revision.
The 64-GPU training and PTX comparisons have not been repeated on this base.

Extract ResolveCudnnSupport and fail on uncompiled cuDNN ops

Extract `ResolveCudnnSupport` into `xla/service/gpu/cudnn_support_utils.h` and lazily resolve `se::dnn::DnnSupport*` inside `CuDnnFusionCompiler` and `CuDnnCustomCallCompiler` only when a cuDNN fusion or custom call is actually encountered.

display_title: [XLA] Add BackendConfigWrapper::content_id()

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add BackendConfigWrapper::content_id()

Backends derive values from backend configs on hot paths, and custom calls that
embed a kernel carry configs of several megabytes. A cache of derived values
must notice when a config changes. The address of the wrapper cannot tell,
because ApplyFnOnProto mutates the wrapper in place.
BackendConfigWrapper::content_id() returns an id of the current contents that
changes whenever they change, and ids are never reused.
HloInstruction::backend_config_content_id() exposes it, so backends can key
caches of derived values by it.

display_title: Report estimated custom-call costs in XProf op metrics.

head_commit.message:
Report estimated custom-call costs in XProf op metrics.
TPU profiles can carry an estimated cost for custom calls that is derived from low-level (LLO) instruction tracing. It is reported as per-event `estimated_flops` and `estimated_bytes_accessed` stats, separately from the compiler or user-annotated cost in the `flops` and `bytes_accessed` event metadata stats.
Accumulate these per-event estimates into new `estimated_flops` and `estimated_bytes_accessed` fields in `OpMetrics` and `FlatOpMetrics`, and carry them through op merging, TF-op aggregation and the `OpMetricsDb` and `FlatOpMetricsDb` combiners.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000754145

head_commit.message:
Plumb BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto into CublasLtMatmulThunk

`CublasLtMatmulThunk` previously only passed `algorithm_idx` when looking up or creating a cached `MatmulPlan`.

Therefore this change threads `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` from `GemmBackendConfig` through `ThunkEmitter` and `CublasLtMatmulThunkProto` into `CublasLtMatmulThunk`. It also adds the `--xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm` debug option so callers can require exact algorithm descriptor reconstruction instead of falling back to the heuristic algorithm index.

display_title: [XLA] Add C++17, IR invariant, and PR preparation guidelines to xla/AGENTS.md and docs/contributing.md.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add C++17, IR invariant, and PR preparation guidelines to xla/AGENTS.md and docs/contributing.md.

**Status quo**
`xla/AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributing.md` cover baseline coding rules and review procedures, while several C++17 compatibility constraints, deterministic iteration rules, HLO/MLIR metadata preservation invariants, unit test assertion requirements, and reproducer-first PR workflows live only in separate internal review skills.

**Why**
Adding the missing rules directly to `xla/AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributing.md`—while keeping the repo-root `AGENTS.md` as a short pointer—gives coding agents and contributors the full set of XLA review and PR preparation standards without duplicating existing documentation or bloating the root `AGENTS.md`.

**Design choices**
- Keep repo-root `AGENTS.md` concise and link to `xla/AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributing.md`.
- Add strict `-std=c++17` pitfalls, deterministic hash iteration, HLO metadata/`OriginalValue` preservation, corner-case shape handling, MLIR module/symbol-table rules, compatibility pointers, and GoogleMock status/decision assertion guidance to `xla/AGENTS.md`.
- Add the reproducer-first bugfix workflow, PR title/description structure, and cross-repository patch guidance to `docs/contributing.md`.

**Compromises**
- None.

**Alternatives**
- Duplicating the full guide in the repo-root `AGENTS.md` was rejected because it duplicates `xla/AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributing.md` and increases always-on system prompt context on every turn.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008031582

display_title: Propagate BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto through CublasLtBackend autotuner

head_commit.message:
Propagate BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto through CublasLtBackend autotuner

Previously `AutotuneResult::GemmKey` and `GemmBackendConfig` only recorded the heuristic algorithm index for cuBLASLt GEMMs.

This change adds an optional `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` field to `AutotuneResult::GemmKey` and `GemmBackendConfig` and updates `CublasLtBackend` to populate and apply the algorithm descriptor proto during autotuning. This way the selected cuBLASLt algorithm configuration is preserved in the HLO backend config instead of relying solely on the heuristic index.

display_title: Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

head_commit.message:
Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

Heuristic indices returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` depend on the GPU and cuBLASLt version, so the same index can resolve to a different kernel across devices or library updates.

Therefore this change introduces `CublasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` (along with their proto definitions in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cublas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto` and `xla/stream_executor/gpu/blas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto`) to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` implements `GetBlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `GetMatmulAlgorithm` to extract and reconstruct `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptors, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` and `BlasLt::GetOrCreateMatmulPlanWithAlgorithm` add overloads accepting `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm`.

head_commit.message:
PR #50805: [XLA:GPU] Record scheduler cost estimates in the HLO

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50805

📝 Summary of Changes

Saves the cost estimates used by the scheduler and their provenance into op metadata of the optimised HLO.
Metadata should not enter any hashes/fingerprints that are required to be stable, but this is initially under a flag to provide an escape hatch in case of bugs.

🎯 Justification

It can be hard to figure out why the scheduler makes decisions; this provides some visibility and makes it easier to evaluate from profiles whether the costs assumed during scheduling were accurate estimates of the final achieved performance.

display_title: Extract ResolveCudnnSupport and fail on uncompiled cuDNN ops

head_commit.message:
Extract ResolveCudnnSupport and fail on uncompiled cuDNN ops

Extract `ResolveCudnnSupport` into `xla/service/gpu/cudnn_support_utils.h` and lazily resolve `se::dnn::DnnSupport*` inside `CuDnnFusionCompiler` and `CuDnnCustomCallCompiler` only when a cuDNN fusion or custom call is actually encountered.

Before this change, compiling devicelessly without cuDNN deviceless compilation enabled would silently skip CuDnnFusionCompiler. Compilation succeeded, but the resulting executable failed at runtime when it tried to deserialize the cuDNN graph. With this change, we fail at compile time instead.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Switch One-Shot Triton AllGather to push-based scratch writes.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Switch One-Shot Triton AllGather to push-based scratch writes.

  * Scratch buffer is now sized based on output instead of input.
  * Instead of each rank pulling subtiles from peer input buffers over NVLink now
    we push the entire tile to peer scratch.
  * This improves 16 device AllGather latency by 1.20x-1.48x across 1 KiB-16 MiB
  * Raises `kMaxAllGatherSizeBytes` from 16 MiB to 32 MiB

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator

    we push the entire tile to peer scratch.
  * This improves 16 device AllGather latency by 1.20x-1.48x across 1 KiB-16 MiB
  * Raises `kMaxAllGatherSizeBytes` from 16 MiB to 32 MiB

display_title: [XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

We have two flags: one enables fast buffer assignment with the fallback
(`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_enable_fast_merge_fallback`), and the other
specifies the buffer assignment algorithm (`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`).

With the fallback enabled, the algorithm for AssignBuffersWithSequentialOrdering specified via `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm` is now the first one to try, and it defines the fallback chain. Previously, enabling the fallback led to not respecting `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`.

The last step of the chain used DEFAULT (= BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL), which always runs the heap simulation twice. It is now split into SPATIAL and then TEMPORAL. **Since the fallback keeps the assignment with the lowest memory usage for each memory space, reaching TEMPORAL gives the same result as BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL, but TEMPORAL is skipped if SPATIAL already fits.**

The pairs below are (non-sequential, sequential) algorithms. Depending on `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`:

* auto, FAST_MERGE: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_MERGE) → (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* FAST_SPLIT: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* SPATIAL: (FAST_MERGE, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, TEMPORAL) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* DEFAULT, BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, X) → (SPATIAL, X)

`AssignmentAlgorithmForComputationsWithoutOrderingProto::DEFAULT` is renamed to `SPATIAL`: like the sequential SPATIAL, it assigns the biggest buffers first.

Only the memory spaces that exceed their memory limit (on TPU, HBM) are reassigned by the fallback steps. The other memory spaces (e.g. VMEM) keep the first assignment, as before.

**If the fallback flag is disabled, we respect the specified algorithm, and
nothing changes.**

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008000977

head_commit.message:
PR #51622: [XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51622

📝 Summary of Changes

Profiled costs now use the `scheduling_name` rather than the final name, adding some tolerance for post-scheduling renames (e.g. ConvertAsyncCollectivesToSync).

AllocateBuffer custom calls only reserve a buffer and launch nothing, so they never appear in a profile. The GPU scheduler now treats them as no-ops, so they are not reported missing and their assumed cost is 0, not 1ms.

No cost is expected for the condition of a while loop with a known trip count, which the GPU runtime never evaluates, so the GPU profile statistics aggregator no longer reports its instructions as missing.

🎯 Justification

Improves PGLE and scheduling accuracy.
Together with other open changes, this reaches full PGLE coverage of DSv3 training.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

`compiler/xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo/`.

  after scheduling rename instructions (e.g. ConvertAsyncCollectivesToSync),
  so e.g. a synchronous all-reduce in the profile was not found when
  compiling again.
- AllocateBuffer custom calls only reserve a buffer and launch nothing, so
  they never appear in a profile. The GPU scheduler treats them as no-ops:
  they are not reported as missing, and their fallback cost is 0 rather than
  the 1000 us of a generic custom call (524 such instructions per DeepSeek-v3
  training step, i.e. 0.5 s of fictitious compute the scheduler believed it
  could hide collectives behind).
- No cost is expected for the condition of a while loop with a known trip
  count, which the GPU runtime never evaluates, so the GPU profile statistics
  aggregator no longer reports its instructions as missing.

Merging this change closes #51622

display_title: [XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

We have two flags: one enables fast buffer assignment with the fallback
(`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_enable_fast_merge_fallback`), and the other
specifies the buffer assignment algorithm (`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`).

With the fallback enabled, the algorithm for AssignBuffersWithSequentialOrdering specified via `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm` is now the first one to try, and it defines the fallback chain. Previously, enabling the fallback led to not respecting `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`.

The last step of the chain used DEFAULT (= BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL), which always runs the heap simulation twice. It is now split into SPATIAL and then TEMPORAL. **Since the fallback keeps the assignment with the lowest memory usage for each memory space, reaching TEMPORAL gives the same result as BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL, but TEMPORAL is skipped if SPATIAL already fits.**

The pairs below are (non-sequential, sequential) algorithms. Depending on `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`:

* auto, FAST_MERGE: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_MERGE) → (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* FAST_SPLIT: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* SPATIAL: (FAST_MERGE, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, TEMPORAL) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* DEFAULT, BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, X) → (SPATIAL, X)

`AssignmentAlgorithmForComputationsWithoutOrderingProto::DEFAULT` is renamed to `SPATIAL`: like the sequential SPATIAL, it assigns the biggest buffers first.

Only the memory spaces that exceed their memory limit (on TPU, HBM) are reassigned by the fallback steps. The other memory spaces (e.g. VMEM) keep the first assignment, as before.

**If the fallback flag is disabled, we respect the specified algorithm, and
nothing changes.**

PiperOrigin-RevId: 998557925

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accumulate `changed` across loops in DoubleBufferLoopUnrolling

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accumulate `changed` across loops in DoubleBufferLoopUnrolling

RunImpl assigned each loop's result to `changed` instead of OR-ing it in.
With the auto strategy, a loop without collectives processed after an
unrolled one reset `changed` to false, so FlattenCallGraph was skipped and
nested loops in the unrolled body were left with several callers. That later
fails the "Call graph must have been flattened" CHECK in
LoopScheduleLinearizer.

Fixes #51687

display_title: Bump c-ares from 1.34.6.bcr.1 to 1.34.6.bcr.3 in MODULE.bazel.

head_commit.message:
Bump c-ares from 1.34.6.bcr.1 to 1.34.6.bcr.3 in MODULE.bazel.

The Bazel Central Registry yanked `c-ares` versions `1.34.6`, `1.34.6.bcr.1`, and `1.34.6.bcr.2` (https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel-central-registry/pull/11392) because those module versions packaged the `1.34.5` sources rather than `1.34.6` (CVE-2025-62408), causing Bzlmod dependency resolution to fail across XLA builds.

Upgrade `c-ares` in `MODULE.bazel` to `1.34.6.bcr.3`, which points to the actual `1.34.6` release sources and satisfies `grpc@1.81.0`'s `c-ares` requirement (`1.19.1`).

display_title: PR #50683: [XLA:GPU] Set max_total_seq_len for packed cuDNN flash attention backward

head_commit.message:
PR #50683: [XLA:GPU] Set max_total_seq_len for packed cuDNN flash attention backward

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50683

📝 Summary of Changes

`GetCudnnFlashAttentionBackwardOperationGraph` now tells cuDNN the maximum packed token count for packed (ragged) SDPA backward. When `max_seg_per_batch` > 1, it computes `max_total_seq_len_q = B * S_q` and `max_total_seq_len_kv = B * S_kv`. It passes them to the graph via `set_max_total_seq_len_q` and `set_max_total_seq_len_kv`. Dense and padding-only graphs are unchanged.

🎯 Justification

For packed graphs, Q/K/V/dO/O/dQ/dK/dV are declared as shape `[B, H, S, D]` with additional attribute `max_seg_per_batch` in XLA to indicate how many segments are packed inside each batch. Without this setting, cuDNN sizes the backward workspace for `B * max_seg_per_batch * S` tokens. The real token count cannot exceed `B * S`, because each of the B physical rows holds at most S tokens. The two dominant workspace terms, `softmax_sum` and the FP32 `dQ_accum`, scale with this token count and shrink by a factor of `max_seg_per_batch`.

Workloads that benefit: packed or segmented-sequence attention training, such as JAX/Flax/MaxText with `max_segments_per_batch` > 1, where backward workspace is often the peak-memory driver.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

🧪 Unit Tests:

cudnn_flash_attention_test.cc

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Clean up legacy symbolic tile analysis workarounds and TODOs.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Clean up legacy symbolic tile analysis workarounds and TODOs.

After removing `SymbolicTileAnalysis` and moving `TilingSpace` out of `experimental`, several legacy workarounds, stale diagnostic messages, and inconsistent constraint checks remained in the XLA:GPU tiling and Triton codegen pipelines:

- Remove the legacy trivial-dimension reshape workaround in `EmitTiledBroadcastedReshape` and the redundant accumulator type cast in `EmitSingleTileDot`, since `TilingSpace` always clamps trivial dimensions to size 1 and `EmitStableHloDotAndAdd` preserves the accumulator type.

- Update `VerifyTritonConstraints` to enforce `kMaxMMADimSize` on `kScaledDot` instructions (matching `VerifySubsetOfTritonConstraints`) and deduplicate `Tile` instances before checking `kMaxTensorNumElements`.

- Replace remaining `SymbolicTileAnalysis` references in fusion diagnostics with `TilingSpace` and remove obsolete `TODO` comments and dead legacy tests.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007938596

head_commit.message:
PR #51639: [XLA:GPU] Fix reading the module fingerprint when creating instruction profiles

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51639

📝 Summary of Changes

Fix reading the pre-scheduling module fingerprint when generating instruction costs from profiles. This fixes the fingerprint prefixing of instruction names and removes ambiguity. Refactor to use shared helpers to avoid inconsistencies creeping back in. Add an extra argument that JAX can use to opt into strict checking that fingerprints are available.

🎯 Justification

This was broken by 7dfb91f0. I intend to make a change in JAX that will cause profiles collected for PGLE to contain multiple executables.

🐛 Bug Fix

n/a

Updated to use now-shared helpers.

n/a

display_title: Bump c-ares from 1.34.6.bcr.1 to 1.34.6.bcr.3 in MODULE.bazel.

head_commit.message:
Bump c-ares from 1.34.6.bcr.1 to 1.34.6.bcr.3 in MODULE.bazel.

The Bazel Central Registry yanked `c-ares` versions `1.34.6`, `1.34.6.bcr.1`, and `1.34.6.bcr.2` (https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel-central-registry/pull/11392) because those module versions packaged the `1.34.5` sources rather than `1.34.6` (CVE-2025-62408), causing Bzlmod dependency resolution to fail across XLA builds.

Upgrade `c-ares` in `MODULE.bazel` to `1.34.6.bcr.3`, which points to the actual `1.34.6` release sources and satisfies `grpc@1.81.0`'s `c-ares` requirement (`1.19.1`).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007958909

head_commit.message:
PR #50805: [XLA:GPU] Record scheduler cost estimates in the HLO

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50805

📝 Summary of Changes

Saves the cost estimates used by the scheduler and their provenance into op metadata of the optimised HLO.
Metadata should not enter any hashes/fingerprints that are required to be stable, but this is initially under a flag to provide an escape hatch in case of bugs.

🎯 Justification

It can be hard to figure out why the scheduler makes decisions; this provides some visibility and makes it easier to evaluate from profiles whether the costs assumed during scheduling were accurate estimates of the final achieved performance.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

display_title: Emit unique kernel symbols for deduplicated fusions under Nsight Compute or debug/line info

head_commit.message:
Emit unique kernel symbols for deduplicated fusions under Nsight Compute or debug/line info

When profiling CUDA Graphs in Nsight Compute (`ncu --graph-profiling node`), build-time NVTX ranges are ignored and kernel targeting via `ncu --kernel-name` relies on the kernel symbol name. When `HloComputationDeduplicator` and `KernelReuseCache` merge identical fusions into a single deduplicated kernel symbol, `ncu` cannot isolate an individual HLO fusion instance.

Skip fusion deduplication in `HloComputationDeduplicator` and include the fusion name in `KernelReuseCache` lookup keys when `xla_gpu_generate_debug_info` or `xla_gpu_generate_line_info` is enabled, or when Nsight Compute environment variables are active.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007276859

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

Copybara import of the project:

With the VMM allocator, pinned_host buffers got device memory with no
CPU mapping, so any CPU access segfaulted (orbax checkpoint saves, for
example). Command buffer update modes other than ALWAYS_UPDATE force

The PJRT GPU client now passes the VMM allocator the same pinned host
allocators the BFC path uses, through the generic

Without a host allocator, MemorySpace::kHost now fails with

Plumb BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto into CublasLtMatmulThunk

`CublasLtMatmulThunk` previously only passed `algorithm_idx` when looking up or creating a cached `MatmulPlan`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Increase default xla_gpu_fusion_autotune_top_k_configs from 1 to 10.

The GPU fusion autotuner's block-level emitter backend previously considered only the single top-ranked candidate tiling config from the indexing performance model (`xla_gpu_fusion_autotune_top_k_configs = 1`). Because analytical cost estimates can diverge from measured kernel execution times on real hardware, evaluating only a single candidate prevents autotuning from selecting faster alternative tilings.

Update `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` in `xla/debug_options_flags.cc` to set `xla_gpu_fusion_autotune_top_k_configs` to 10 by default, and add a unit test in `xla/debug_options_flags_test.cc` verifying the new default.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007937722

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

display_title: PR #51488: [XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

head_commit.message:
PR #51488: [XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51488

## Summary

`xla.atomic_rmw` can contain `subf(current, x)` after arithmetic
canonicalization. `GetAtomicModifierParameters` had no case for that form.
The CAS fallback handled those atomics, and jax-ml/jax#41467 reports the
resulting slowdown in scatter and segment reductions.

This change handles `subf(current, x)` as `fadd(current, -x)`. The negate
is emitted before the direct atomic and inside the vectorized yield.
Modifiers defined inside the atomic body are rejected. `subf(x, current)`
and `subf(current, current)` are not representable as an atomic add and
still use the CAS fallback. The two-op paths also require the body to yield
the modifier result; otherwise they fall back to CAS.

## Tests

`//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms/tests:tests` passes 25/25. Tests cover
scalar f32/f16, widened bf16, swapped and in-body operands, vectorized f32,
Pascal/Ampere fallback, AMD packed f16/bf16, SPIR-V, and f8 fallback.

I built XLA for CUDA 12.9 on an sm_120 GPU and compiled the issue HLO with
valid literals. The unpatched lowering emits a `cmpxchg` loop, the patched
lowering emits `atom.global.v4.f32.add`, and the GPU result matches the
interpreter.

## Performance

The issue reports these times on an RTX 3090: 0.50 ms with jaxlib 0.11.0,
10.37 ms with 0.11.1, and 10.22 ms with 0.11.2. The same pattern on an
RTX 5060 measures 1.26 ms with 0.11.0 and 6.13 ms with 0.11.2. The 0.11.0
kernel emits `atom.global.v4.f32.add`; the regressed kernel emits a
`cmpxchg` loop.

I ran both compilers on the same RTX 5060 with CUDA 12.9 and sm_120 using
`hlo_runner_main_gpu`. The numbers are means of 50 repeats after the warmup
call; the one-group case uses 20 repeats.

Reporter HLO:

| lowering | time per call |
| --- | --- |
| unpatched | 3.62 ms |
| patched | 0.096 ms |

Contention sweep:

| groups | unpatched | patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 group | 358.4 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 64 groups, 90% to one group | 309.4 ms | 0.129 ms |
| 8 groups, uniform | 23.91 ms | 0.076 ms |
| 64 groups, uniform | 1.458 ms | 0.021 ms |
| 64 groups, round-robin | 1.189 ms | 0.020 ms |
| 1024 groups, uniform | 0.140 ms | 0.021 ms |
| 2048 groups, uniform | 0.092 ms | 0.027 ms |
| 4096 groups, uniform | 0.085 ms | 0.020 ms |

The reporter HLO is the module generated by the JAX repro, dumped before
XLA optimization. `hlo_runner_main_gpu` runs the normal optimization
pipeline on it. The file includes the actual scatter indices. The sweep uses
single-scatter HLOs with 65,536x32 updates. The one-group case sends every
update to one group; the hotspot case sends 90% to one group.

Treat subf(current, x) as fadd(current, -x) in atomic RMW lowering, including the vectorized path. Reject modifiers defined inside the atomic body.

Merging this change closes #51488

PR #50683: [XLA:GPU] Set max_total_seq_len for packed cuDNN flash attention backward

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50683

📝 Summary of Changes

`GetCudnnFlashAttentionBackwardOperationGraph` now tells cuDNN the maximum packed token count for packed (ragged) SDPA backward. When `max_seg_per_batch` > 1, it computes `max_total_seq_len_q = B * S_q` and `max_total_seq_len_kv = B * S_kv`. It passes them to the graph via `set_max_total_seq_len_q` and `set_max_total_seq_len_kv`. Dense and padding-only graphs are unchanged.

🎯 Justification

For packed graphs, Q/K/V/dO/O/dQ/dK/dV are declared as shape `[B, H, S, D]` with additional attribute `max_seg_per_batch` in XLA to indicate how many segments are packed inside each batch. Without this setting, cuDNN sizes the backward workspace for `B * max_seg_per_batch * S` tokens. The real token count cannot exceed `B * S`, because each of the B physical rows holds at most S tokens. The two dominant workspace terms, `softmax_sum` and the FP32 `dQ_accum`, scale with this token count and shrink by a factor of `max_seg_per_batch`.

Workloads that benefit: packed or segmented-sequence attention training, such as JAX/Flax/MaxText with `max_segments_per_batch` > 1, where backward workspace is often the peak-memory driver.

head_commit.message:
PR #50069: [ROCm] Fall back to an unfused FP8 conversion when hipBLASLt has no kernel

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50069

## Motivation

hipBLASLt's kernel coverage for FP8 outputs differs between GPUs and library releases. Today an FP8-output GEMM that hipBLASLt has no algorithm for fails to compile with "No supported configs found". This adds an autotuner fallback that runs it with a wider output and converts to FP8 separately.

Part of a series: depends on #50068, which adds `GemmBackendConfig.has_d_scale` (its commit is included here until it lands). Independent of #49829, the FP8 output fusion on ROCm.

## Details

- When hipBLASLt returns no algorithm for an FP8-output `__cublas$lt$matmul$f8`, `HipblasLtBackend` offers the algorithms of a wider-output copy, marked by a new `GemmKey.unfuse_fp8_output`. `ApplyConfig` rewrites the call into that GEMM plus a loop fusion for the D scale, saturating clamp and conversion.
- The fallback is offered only when the fused query is empty, so fused kernels are never displaced. `HIPBLASLT_FISSION` gets it through its inner backend, and cached or AOT results replay it without a device.
- It logs a warning when it fires, like the MX path.
- Limitation: deviceless/AOT compiles without autotune results can't query hipBLASLt, so a missing kernel there still fails at run time.

## Test Plan

On gfx950, ran `hipblaslt_test` (fallback offered only without fused algorithms, including a D-scaled mixed-input GEMM, plus the rewrite) and `gemm_rewriter_fp8_test` (forced fallback for an FP8 dot, executed against the reference), along with the other ROCm GEMM tests.

## Test Result

All pass on gfx950.

display_title: Propagate BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto through CublasLtBackend autotuner

head_commit.message:
Propagate BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto through CublasLtBackend autotuner

Previously `AutotuneResult::GemmKey` and `GemmBackendConfig` only recorded the heuristic algorithm index for cuBLASLt GEMMs.

This change adds an optional `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` field to `AutotuneResult::GemmKey` and `GemmBackendConfig` and updates `CublasLtBackend` to populate and apply the algorithm descriptor proto during autotuning. This way the selected cuBLASLt algorithm configuration is preserved in the HLO backend config instead of relying solely on the heuristic index.

display_title: Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

head_commit.message:
Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

Heuristic indices returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` depend on the GPU and cuBLASLt version, so the same index can resolve to a different kernel across devices or library updates.

Therefore this change introduces `CublasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` (along with their proto definitions in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cublas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto` and `xla/stream_executor/gpu/blas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto`) to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` implements `GetBlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `GetMatmulAlgorithm` to extract and reconstruct `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptors, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` and `BlasLt::GetOrCreateMatmulPlanWithAlgorithm` add overloads accepting `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005556772
