head_commit.message:
Plumb BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto into CublasLtMatmulThunk

`CublasLtMatmulThunk` previously only passed `algorithm_idx` when looking up or creating a cached `MatmulPlan`.

Therefore this change threads `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` from `GemmBackendConfig` through `ThunkEmitter` and `CublasLtMatmulThunkProto` into `CublasLtMatmulThunk`. It also adds the `--xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm` debug option so callers can require exact algorithm descriptor reconstruction instead of falling back to the heuristic algorithm index.

display_title: PR #51622: [XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

head_commit.message:
PR #51622: [XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51622

📝 Summary of Changes

Profiled costs now use the `scheduling_name` rather than the final name, adding some tolerance for post-scheduling renames (e.g. ConvertAsyncCollectivesToSync).

AllocateBuffer custom calls only reserve a buffer and launch nothing, so they never appear in a profile. The GPU scheduler now treats them as no-ops, so they are not reported missing and their assumed cost is 0, not 1ms.

No cost is expected for the condition of a while loop with a known trip count, which the GPU runtime never evaluates, so the GPU profile statistics aggregator no longer reports its instructions as missing.

🎯 Justification

Improves PGLE and scheduling accuracy.
Together with other open changes, this reaches full PGLE coverage of DSv3 training.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Please measure and include speedups for one of the public HLOs in
`compiler/xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo/`.

🧪 Unit Tests:

Added.

🧪 Execution Tests:

n/a

eedcbdcbd05058351cd8a135043da548ffea3279 by Olli Lupton <olupton@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

- Profiled costs are keyed by the instruction's OpMetadata.scheduling_name,
  the name the scheduler knew it by, rather than by its final name. Passes
  after scheduling rename instructions (e.g. ConvertAsyncCollectivesToSync),
  so e.g. a synchronous all-reduce in the profile was not found when
  compiling again.
- AllocateBuffer custom calls only reserve a buffer and launch nothing, so
  they never appear in a profile. The GPU scheduler treats them as no-ops:
  they are not reported as missing, and their fallback cost is 0 rather than
  the 1000 us of a generic custom call (524 such instructions per DeepSeek-v3
  training step, i.e. 0.5 s of fictitious compute the scheduler believed it
  could hide collectives behind).
- No cost is expected for the condition of a while loop with a known trip
  count, which the GPU runtime never evaluates, so the GPU profile statistics
  aggregator no longer reports its instructions as missing.

Merging this change closes #51622

display_title: PR #51488: [XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

head_commit.message:
PR #51488: [XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51488

## Summary

`xla.atomic_rmw` can contain `subf(current, x)` after arithmetic
canonicalization. `GetAtomicModifierParameters` had no case for that form.
The CAS fallback handled those atomics, and jax-ml/jax#41467 reports the
resulting slowdown in scatter and segment reductions.

This change handles `subf(current, x)` as `fadd(current, -x)`. The negate
is emitted before the direct atomic and inside the vectorized yield.
Modifiers defined inside the atomic body are rejected. `subf(x, current)`
and `subf(current, current)` are not representable as an atomic add and
still use the CAS fallback. The two-op paths also require the body to yield
the modifier result; otherwise they fall back to CAS.

## Tests

`//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms/tests:tests` passes 25/25. Tests cover
scalar f32/f16, widened bf16, swapped and in-body operands, vectorized f32,
Pascal/Ampere fallback, AMD packed f16/bf16, SPIR-V, and f8 fallback.

I built XLA for CUDA 12.9 on an sm_120 GPU and compiled the issue HLO with
valid literals. The unpatched lowering emits a `cmpxchg` loop, the patched
lowering emits `atom.global.v4.f32.add`, and the GPU result matches the
interpreter.

## Performance

The issue reports these times on an RTX 3090: 0.50 ms with jaxlib 0.11.0,
10.37 ms with 0.11.1, and 10.22 ms with 0.11.2. The same pattern on an
RTX 5060 measures 1.26 ms with 0.11.0 and 6.13 ms with 0.11.2. The 0.11.0
kernel emits `atom.global.v4.f32.add`; the regressed kernel emits a
`cmpxchg` loop.

I ran both compilers on the same RTX 5060 with CUDA 12.9 and sm_120 using
`hlo_runner_main_gpu`. The numbers are means of 50 repeats after the warmup
call; the one-group case uses 20 repeats.

Reporter HLO:

| lowering | time per call |
| --- | --- |
| unpatched | 3.62 ms |
| patched | 0.096 ms |

Contention sweep:

| groups | unpatched | patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 group | 358.4 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 64 groups, 90% to one group | 309.4 ms | 0.129 ms |
| 8 groups, uniform | 23.91 ms | 0.076 ms |
| 64 groups, uniform | 1.458 ms | 0.021 ms |
| 64 groups, round-robin | 1.189 ms | 0.020 ms |
| 1024 groups, uniform | 0.140 ms | 0.021 ms |
| 2048 groups, uniform | 0.092 ms | 0.027 ms |
| 4096 groups, uniform | 0.085 ms | 0.020 ms |

The reporter HLO is the module generated by the JAX repro, dumped before
XLA optimization. `hlo_runner_main_gpu` runs the normal optimization
pipeline on it. The file includes the actual scatter indices. The sweep uses
single-scatter HLOs with 65,536x32 updates. The one-group case sends every
update to one group; the hotspot case sends 90% to one group.

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

[ROCm] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator

With the VMM allocator, pinned_host buffers got device memory with no
CPU mapping, so any CPU access segfaulted (orbax checkpoint saves, for
example). Command buffer update modes other than ALWAYS_UPDATE force
the VMM allocator, so they were affected too.

The PJRT GPU client now passes the VMM allocator the same pinned host
allocators the BFC path uses, through the generic
DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create() with no CUDA/ROCm #if branches.
Without a host allocator, MemorySpace::kHost now fails with

[ROCm] Keep the VMM allocator factory dep of se_gpu_pjrt_client_impl

The factory target exports no headers, so dependency cleanup sees it as
unused and drops it, which leaves DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()
undefined at link time.

Merging this change closes #50583

display_title: PR #51488: [XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

head_commit.message:
PR #51488: [XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51488

## Summary

`xla.atomic_rmw` can contain `subf(current, x)` after arithmetic
canonicalization. `GetAtomicModifierParameters` had no case for that form.
The CAS fallback handled those atomics, and jax-ml/jax#41467 reports the
resulting slowdown in scatter and segment reductions.

This change handles `subf(current, x)` as `fadd(current, -x)`. The negate
is emitted before the direct atomic and inside the vectorized yield.
Modifiers defined inside the atomic body are rejected. `subf(x, current)`
and `subf(current, current)` are not representable as an atomic add and
still use the CAS fallback. The two-op paths also require the body to yield
the modifier result; otherwise they fall back to CAS.

## Tests

`//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms/tests:tests` passes 25/25. Tests cover
scalar f32/f16, widened bf16, swapped and in-body operands, vectorized f32,
Pascal/Ampere fallback, AMD packed f16/bf16, SPIR-V, and f8 fallback.

I built XLA for CUDA 12.9 on an sm_120 GPU and compiled the issue HLO with
valid literals. The unpatched lowering emits a `cmpxchg` loop, the patched
lowering emits `atom.global.v4.f32.add`, and the GPU result matches the
interpreter.

## Performance

The issue reports these times on an RTX 3090: 0.50 ms with jaxlib 0.11.0,
10.37 ms with 0.11.1, and 10.22 ms with 0.11.2. The same pattern on an
RTX 5060 measures 1.26 ms with 0.11.0 and 6.13 ms with 0.11.2. The 0.11.0
kernel emits `atom.global.v4.f32.add`; the regressed kernel emits a
`cmpxchg` loop.

I ran both compilers on the same RTX 5060 with CUDA 12.9 and sm_120 using
`hlo_runner_main_gpu`. The numbers are means of 50 repeats after the warmup
call; the one-group case uses 20 repeats.

Reporter HLO:

| lowering | time per call |
| --- | --- |
| unpatched | 3.62 ms |
| patched | 0.096 ms |

Contention sweep:

| groups | unpatched | patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 group | 358.4 ms | 0.141 ms |
| 64 groups, 90% to one group | 309.4 ms | 0.129 ms |
| 8 groups, uniform | 23.91 ms | 0.076 ms |
| 64 groups, uniform | 1.458 ms | 0.021 ms |
| 64 groups, round-robin | 1.189 ms | 0.020 ms |
| 1024 groups, uniform | 0.140 ms | 0.021 ms |
| 2048 groups, uniform | 0.092 ms | 0.027 ms |
| 4096 groups, uniform | 0.085 ms | 0.020 ms |

The reporter HLO is the module generated by the JAX repro, dumped before
XLA optimization. `hlo_runner_main_gpu` runs the normal optimization
pipeline on it. The file includes the actual scatter indices. The sweep uses
single-scatter HLOs with 65,536x32 updates. The one-group case sends every
update to one group; the hotspot case sends 90% to one group.

display_title: PR #50069: [ROCm] Fall back to an unfused FP8 conversion when hipBLASLt has no kernel

head_commit.message:
PR #50069: [ROCm] Fall back to an unfused FP8 conversion when hipBLASLt has no kernel

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50069

## Motivation

hipBLASLt's kernel coverage for FP8 outputs differs between GPUs and library releases. Today an FP8-output GEMM that hipBLASLt has no algorithm for fails to compile with "No supported configs found". This adds an autotuner fallback that runs it with a wider output and converts to FP8 separately.

Part of a series: depends on #50068, which adds `GemmBackendConfig.has_d_scale` (its commit is included here until it lands). Independent of #49829, the FP8 output fusion on ROCm.

## Details

- When hipBLASLt returns no algorithm for an FP8-output `__cublas$lt$matmul$f8`, `HipblasLtBackend` offers the algorithms of a wider-output copy, marked by a new `GemmKey.unfuse_fp8_output`. `ApplyConfig` rewrites the call into that GEMM plus a loop fusion for the D scale, saturating clamp and conversion.
- The fallback is offered only when the fused query is empty, so fused kernels are never displaced. `HIPBLASLT_FISSION` gets it through its inner backend, and cached or AOT results replay it without a device.
- It logs a warning when it fires, like the MX path.
- Limitation: deviceless/AOT compiles without autotune results can't query hipBLASLt, so a missing kernel there still fails at run time.

## Test Plan

On gfx950, ran `hipblaslt_test` (fallback offered only without fused algorithms, including a D-scaled mixed-input GEMM, plus the rewrite) and `gemm_rewriter_fp8_test` (forced fallback for an FP8 dot, executed against the reference), along with the other ROCm GEMM tests.

## Test Result

All pass on gfx950.

display_title: Emit unique kernel symbols for deduplicated fusions under Nsight Compute or debug/line info

head_commit.message:
Emit unique kernel symbols for deduplicated fusions under Nsight Compute or debug/line info

When profiling CUDA Graphs in Nsight Compute (`ncu --graph-profiling node`), build-time NVTX ranges are ignored and kernel targeting via `ncu --kernel-name` relies on the kernel symbol name. When `HloComputationDeduplicator` and `KernelReuseCache` merge identical fusions into a single deduplicated kernel symbol, `ncu` cannot isolate an individual HLO fusion instance.

Skip fusion deduplication in `HloComputationDeduplicator` and include the fusion name in `KernelReuseCache` lookup keys when `xla_gpu_generate_debug_info` or `xla_gpu_generate_line_info` is enabled, or when Nsight Compute environment variables are active.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse producers into Triton scan fusions with a scan dimension above 128 (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`) when the producer has only effective-scalar operands and consists of only effective-scalar parameters, effective-scalar constants, `iota`, broadcasts of effective scalars, and elementwise operations (`IsCheapNoMemoryProducer`).

Fusing these memoryless producers avoids materializing full-size intermediate broadcast or mask tensors in global memory when a scan has an epilogue that broadcasts scalar thresholds or compares against `iota`. On `f32[256, N]` cumsum with an elementwise epilogue (`N` in `{131072, 262144}`) and `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` enabled, this reduces execution from 3 kernels before this change to 1 kernel, speeding up H100 by 1.7x (230–457 µs to 134–266 µs) and B200 by 2.0x (161–322 µs to 80–156 µs, 2.3x faster than the default emitter).

With default flags, this change has no effect.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007841057

display_title: Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

head_commit.message:
Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

`CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` skips `cuGraphExec*NodeSetParams` for commands with unchanged buffer allocations, leaving update-time NVTX attribution in `nsys-ui` (`CUPTI_CBID_RESOURCE_GRAPHNODE_SET_PARAMS`) incomplete and absent from SQLite `CUDA_GRAPH_NODE_EVENTS` while emitting redundant host NVTX ranges every step. Late-start (`cudaProfilerStart`) node profiling requires `--cuda-graph-trace=node:nvtx-precapture` to attribute all nodes from `RecordCreate` without buffering per-step update ranges during warmup.

Remove the outer `ScopedAnnotation` from `CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` and push it inside the `GetOrTraceCommandBuffer` trace callback in `TracedCommand::RecordTracedCommand` on `RecordUpdate` to preserve child-graph cache-miss attribution.

Previously, `CuptiErrorManager` disabled CUPTI process-wide on this error, `CuptiTracer::EnableApiTracing` set `api_tracing_enabled_` before `PrepareSubscriberForSession` succeeded, and `CuptiTracer::Disable` unconditionally dereferenced uninitialized state.

head_commit.message:
When Nsight Systems or Nsight Compute holds the CUPTI subscriber slot, `cuptiSubscribe` returns `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` (or `CUPTI_ERROR_MAX_LIMIT_REACHED`). Previously, `CuptiErrorManager` disabled CUPTI process-wide on this error, `CuptiTracer::EnableApiTracing` set `api_tracing_enabled_` before `PrepareSubscriberForSession` succeeded, and `CuptiTracer::Disable` unconditionally dereferenced uninitialized state.

Handle external CUPTI subscriber conflicts per session:

- Allow `CUPTI_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES`, `CUPTI_ERROR_MAX_LIMIT_REACHED`, and `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` in `CuptiErrorManager::Subscribe` and `CuptiErrorManager::SubscribeV2` without disabling CUPTI.
- Call `PrepareCallbackStart()` after `PrepareSubscriberForSession()` in `CuptiTracer::EnableApiTracing()`, clear subscriber state, log a warning, and return `absl::UnavailableError`.
- Reset `collector_`, `option_`, and `cupti_driver_api_hook_` on `Enable()` failure, and guard `CuptiTracer::Disable()`.

display_title: Emit unique kernel symbols for deduplicated fusions under Nsight Compute or debug/line info

head_commit.message:
Emit unique kernel symbols for deduplicated fusions under Nsight Compute or debug/line info

When profiling CUDA Graphs in Nsight Compute (`ncu --graph-profiling node`), build-time NVTX ranges are ignored and kernel targeting via `ncu --kernel-name` relies on the kernel symbol name. When `HloComputationDeduplicator` and `KernelReuseCache` merge identical fusions into a single deduplicated kernel symbol, `ncu` cannot isolate an individual HLO fusion instance.

Skip fusion deduplication in `HloComputationDeduplicator` and include the fusion name in `KernelReuseCache` lookup keys when `xla_gpu_generate_debug_info` or `xla_gpu_generate_line_info` is enabled, or when Nsight Compute environment variables are active.

name: CI
display_title: Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

head_commit.message:
Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

`CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` skips `cuGraphExec*NodeSetParams` for commands with unchanged buffer allocations, leaving update-time NVTX attribution in `nsys-ui` (`CUPTI_CBID_RESOURCE_GRAPHNODE_SET_PARAMS`) incomplete and absent from SQLite `CUDA_GRAPH_NODE_EVENTS` while emitting redundant host NVTX ranges every step. Late-start (`cudaProfilerStart`) node profiling requires `--cuda-graph-trace=node:nvtx-precapture` to attribute all nodes from `RecordCreate` without buffering per-step update ranges during warmup.

Remove the outer `ScopedAnnotation` from `CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` and push it inside the `GetOrTraceCommandBuffer` trace callback in `TracedCommand::RecordTracedCommand` on `RecordUpdate` to preserve child-graph cache-miss attribution.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

When one loop iteration reads and then updates a loop-carried buffer in place
several times in a row (e.g. gather + scatter optimizer updates of an embedding
table across unrolled loop steps), CopyInsertion adds a copy before every
in-place op and CopyRemover cannot remove any of them: in each step the copy and
the reader of the previous value are unordered, so removing one step's copy
requires the next step's reader to be ordered before the next copy, and vice
versa.

Add an opt-in CopyInsertion option that orders the other readers of an in-place
operand that are already predecessors of the in-place op before the copy added
for that operand. This does not constrain the schedule beyond what the in-place
op already requires, but gives copy removal the ordering it needs. The option is
only enabled for the TPU copy insertion pass for now.

Tested: new unit tests in copy_insertion_test; on a production embedding model
this removes all embedding-table copies (~1.9 GiB per step program).
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004536340

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

Restrict `ScanRewriterTriton::IsEligibleScan` to skip scans where `AssociativeScanRewriter` combined with native `kLoop` or `kInput` fusions produces fewer kernel launches or better memory coalescing:

1. Require `scan_dim_size > 1` so degenerate single-element scans are left to `AssociativeScanRewriter` instead of launching a Triton kernel.
2. Require the scan dimension to be the most minor physical dimension of the input layout (`LayoutUtil::Minor(input_shape.layout(), 0) == scan_dim`) when a layout is present, ensuring coalesced memory accesses along the scan dimension.
3. Reject small scans (`scan_dim_size <= 1024`) without a `kCustom` fusion producer when their bounded non-effective-scalar producer or consumer neighborhood (walking through elementwise ops, `kBroadcast`, `kBitcast`, and `kReshape`) touches a loop or input data-movement or indexing op (`kConcatenate`, `kDynamicSlice`, `kDynamicUpdateSlice`, `kGather`, `kPad`, `kReverse`, `kScatter`, `kSlice`). For scans up to 3 radix-16 reduction levels, keeping the lowered scan in the surrounding native fusion avoids splitting the fusion around a standalone Triton scan kernel.

With default flags, this change has no effect.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007236560

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse producers into Triton scan fusions with a scan dimension above 128 (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`) when the producer has only effective-scalar operands and consists of only effective-scalar parameters, effective-scalar constants, `iota`, broadcasts of effective scalars, and elementwise operations (`IsCheapNoMemoryProducer`).

Fusing these memoryless producers avoids materializing full-size intermediate broadcast or mask tensors in global memory when a scan has an epilogue that broadcasts scalar thresholds or compares against `iota`. On `f32[256, N]` cumsum with an elementwise epilogue (`N` in `{131072, 262144}`) and `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` enabled, this reduces execution from 3 kernels before this change to 1 kernel, speeding up H100 by 1.7x (230–457 µs to 134–266 µs) and B200 by 2.0x (161–322 µs to 80–156 µs, 2.3x faster than the default emitter).

With default flags, this change has no effect.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007038444

display_title: Lower ApproxTopK fallback to unstable sort on CPU and GPU.

head_commit.message:
Lower ApproxTopK fallback to unstable sort on CPU and GPU.

`ApproxTopK` on TPU already aggregates candidates using an unstable sort (`is_stable=false`), whereas `ApproxTopKFallback` on CPU and GPU previously forced `is_stable=true`. On XLA:GPU, requiring stability routed `approx_top_k` through a 64-bit key/index bit-packing adapter rather than dispatching directly to the native unstable `select_k` kernel.

Switch `ApproxTopKFallback` to emit `is_stable=false`, aligning CPU and GPU semantics with TPU and allowing XLA:GPU to dispatch `approx_top_k` directly to RAFT `select_k` without U64 packing and unpacking overhead.

display_title: [XLA:PJRT] Dispatch HostMemoryUnregister on device dispatch thread.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PJRT] Dispatch HostMemoryUnregister on device dispatch thread.

In multi-GPU workloads on CUDA, `cuMemHostUnregister` (called via `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::DmaUnmap()` or a custom `HostMemoryAllocator`'s `unmap_fn`) may synchronize with the CUDA context that owns the registration, i.e. the first device's (GPU 0's) context. If this happens while GPU 0's dispatch thread is concurrently launching a multi-GPU collective, it can result in a cross-GPU deadlock.

To prevent `HostMemoryUnregister` from running concurrently with multi-GPU collective launches:
- If the device's StreamExecutor reports `HostMemoryUnregisterMaySynchronize()` (currently only CUDA), `LocalDeviceState::HostMemoryUnregister()` schedules `executor_->HostMemoryUnregister(data)` onto `async_dispatch_thread_` (when async dispatch is enabled) or `execute_thread_` (otherwise) and waits for completion, falling back to running inline when already on the dispatch thread or after `LocalDeviceState::Destroy()` has reset the threads during client teardown.
- The `XLA_PJRT_GPU_UNREGISTER_HOST_MEMORY_ON_DISPATCH_THREAD` environment variable overrides the executor's answer, e.g. as a kill switch.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003278628

head_commit.message:
Unify TOTAL and PARTIAL U64 key adapters in XLA:GPU TopkSpecializer.

Based on the U64 pack/unpack deduplication in https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51604 by dimitar-asenov, split out from the `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` heuristic change.

`TopkSpecializer` maintained separate `TOTAL`- and `PARTIAL`-order HLO builders for packing `F32` values with `iota` indices into `U64` priority keys and unpacking them back to `F32`, duplicating the shared IEEE-754 bitwise radix flip/unflip and 64-bit shift-and-merge sequences.
Consolidate the four helpers into `BuildPackF32ToU64` and `BuildUnpackU64ToF32` parameterized by `ComparisonOrder` (guarded with `TF_RET_CHECK` for `kTotal` and `kPartial`), branching only on the reversed index width and `-0.0f` canonicalization/restoration needed for `kPartial` while emitting identical HLO for both orderings.

name: CI
display_title: The latency hiding scheduler accounts for the resources used by the async ops

head_commit.message:
The latency hiding scheduler accounts for the resources used by the async ops
nested in an instruction's called computations as "recursive resources" of
that instruction, checked against the overlap limits when the instruction is
scheduled. For an async op only its start reports the async computation as a
called computation, so those resources were only checked at the start and
never at the update or done. With bottom-up scheduling the done is scheduled
first, so an async op wrapping a computation that uses a resource could be
started while that resource was exhausted, with the scheduler then pushing
other starts in between the async op's start and done.

Account for the async computation at the update and done of an async op as
well, so that the resources used inside it are checked at both ends of it.
Async ops whose computation uses no such resources are unaffected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008447389

display_title: [XLA] Preserve infinite magnitude for complex abs on NaN + Inf*i

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve infinite magnitude for complex abs on NaN + Inf*i

Under IEEE 754 / ISO C99 Annex G (G.5.1 / G.6), if either component of a complex number is infinite, its magnitude is +inf even if the other component is NaN.

EmitComplexAbs, EmitSqrtComplexAbs, and EmitRsqrtComplexAbs previously returned NaN when an input had mixed NaN and Inf components because the Cartesian reduction evaluated to NaN.

Extract EmitComplexAbsSpecialCases to handle special cases for complex magnitude:
- If either component is infinite, return +inf (or 0 for rsqrt).
- Otherwise, if either component is NaN, return NaN.
- If both components are zero, return 0 (or +inf for rsqrt).
- Otherwise, return the computed result (or the fallback under fast-math).

Also clear noNaNs and noInfs under FastMathFlagGuard before emitting the zero comparison to prevent poison values when noNaNs is set without noInfs.

display_title: [Pathways] Canonicalize HLO program names in keys

head_commit.message:
[Pathways] Canonicalize HLO program names in keys

MPMD program stages often compile to identical executables, but their cache
keys differ in the module name and the Shardy mesh names. The new flag
`--pathways_compilation_cache_canonicalize_hlo_program_names`, true by default,
makes keys canonicalize mesh names, and the module name unless TPU flags depend
on it.
Existing single flight deduplication then compiles each distinct stage once.
Stages that share a compilation keep their own IFRT executable names, but their
TPU metadata comes from the compiled program. The flag must match on clients
and servers, and persistent cache keys of named programs change once.

display_title: Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

head_commit.message:
Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` were lowered as large graphs of primitive operations, which made both compilation and execution slow.

This change replaces the CPU implementation of `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` with C++ kernels in a new `_math` extension, vectorized with Highway and parallelized across threads for large arrays. Both kernels keep the same accuracy bounds (`<= 1.0` ULP for `float16`/`float32`/`float64` and `<= 0.5` ULP for `bfloat16`), support sharded execution and `jax.export`, and fix batch partitioning for custom calls when all dimensions are batch dimensions.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Do not pad grouped integer convolutions in CudnnPadForConvolutions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Do not pad grouped integer convolutions in CudnnPadForConvolutions

The integer path padded the kernel input-feature dimension (and the other
feature dimensions) to a multiple of 4 or 32 without looking at
feature_group_count, so the cuDNN custom call kept its group count while
input_features != feature_group_count * kernel_input_features. cuDNN then
silently returned wrong values for part of the output. The f16 path already
skips grouped convolutions for this reason; do the same for integers.

Fixes #49123.

name: CI
display_title: Skip bazel-diff on global Bazel config skew

head_commit.message:
Skip bazel-diff on global Bazel config skew

In GitHub Actions pull request jobs, `actions/checkout` checks out the synthetic merge commit while `build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` checks out the PR's `merge-base` and branch tip. If `main` updated `.bazelversion`, `.bazelrc`, or `MODULE.bazel` after the PR branched, `bazel-diff` starts a Bazel server with older version or startup flags in the shared `output_base`. When the subsequent test step runs on the merge commit and shuts down that server, containers whose PID 1 does not reap child processes leave a zombie server process and Bazel aborts with exit code 36.

Therefore this change checks whether any global Bazel configuration file differs between `head_sha` and the checked-out `HEAD` before invoking Bazel, and falls back to `Decision=FULL` immediately if so. This avoids starting a mismatched Bazel daemon (and avoids failing `cquery` on flags added on `main`) while keeping warm Skyframe reuse when global Bazel configs match.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008333515

[Mosaic] Keep the reduced dimension in tpu.reduce_index

The result of `tpu.reduce_index` now has the rank of its input, with the reduced dimension set to 1, which matches `tpu.reduce`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:PJRT] Dispatch HostMemoryUnregister on device dispatch thread.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PJRT] Dispatch HostMemoryUnregister on device dispatch thread.

In multi-GPU workloads on CUDA, `cuMemHostUnregister` (called via `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::DmaUnmap()` or a custom `HostMemoryAllocator`'s `unmap_fn`) may synchronize with the CUDA context that owns the registration, i.e. the first device's (GPU 0's) context. If this happens while GPU 0's dispatch thread is concurrently launching a multi-GPU collective, it can result in a cross-GPU deadlock.

To prevent `HostMemoryUnregister` from running concurrently with multi-GPU collective launches:
- If the device's StreamExecutor reports `HostMemoryUnregisterMaySynchronize()` (currently only CUDA), `LocalDeviceState::HostMemoryUnregister()` schedules `executor_->HostMemoryUnregister(data)` onto `async_dispatch_thread_` (when async dispatch is enabled) or `execute_thread_` (otherwise) and waits for completion, falling back to running inline when already on the dispatch thread or after `LocalDeviceState::Destroy()` has reset the threads during client teardown.
- The `XLA_PJRT_GPU_UNREGISTER_HOST_MEMORY_ON_DISPATCH_THREAD` environment variable overrides the executor's answer, e.g. as a kill switch.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003278628

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PJRT] Add LocalDeviceState::HostMemoryRegister/Unregister.

- Add `LocalDeviceState::HostMemoryRegister()` and `LocalDeviceState::HostMemoryUnregister()` and use them in `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::DmaMap()`/`DmaUnmap()` and in the custom host memory allocator's `map_fn`/`unmap_fn` created by `GetStreamExecutorGpuClient()`, so that `LocalDeviceState` can control how host memory (un)registration is performed.
- Since the custom host memory allocator's `unmap_fn` now captures the first `LocalDeviceState`, explicitly destroy `host_memory_allocator_` in `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::~PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient()` while `local_device_states_` is still alive.
- Remove the redundant `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::executor_` member (always the first local device's executor) and the corresponding constructor parameters of `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient` and `StreamExecutorGpuRawClient`.

No behavior change intended.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Make ProgramMemoryTracer thread-safe and stop caching its trace.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Make ProgramMemoryTracer thread-safe and stop caching its trace.

`IfrtIrLoadedExecutable::GetIfrtIrProgramMemoryStats()` and
`GetIfrtIrProgramXprofUrl()` are const methods, but both call into
`ProgramMemoryTracer`, which built and cached its memory trace on first use
without synchronization, so concurrent first calls raced. The cached trace,
liveness analysis and topology cache also stayed in host memory for the
executable's lifetime once anyone asked for the stats.

`ProgramMemoryTracer` now guards its state with a mutex. The state built for
a trace lives in one `TraceState` struct that is created on demand and reset
right after use. Only the small results are cached: the memory stats, and the
xprof URL until a day before its xprof session expires. Uploaded sessions now
request an explicit 14-day TTL so that this expiry is known.

Adds a test that queries the memory stats from several threads.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008304544

display_title: [XLA:PJRT] Add LocalDeviceState::Destroy() and DrainDispatchThreads().

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PJRT] Add LocalDeviceState::Destroy() and DrainDispatchThreads().

- Factor `~LocalDeviceState()` teardown into `LocalDeviceState::Destroy()`, and join `execute_thread_` and `async_dispatch_thread_` before `SynchronizeAllActivity()` so that all previously scheduled work has been enqueued onto the streams before they are synchronized.
- Add `LocalDeviceState::DrainDispatchThreads()`, which drains `execute_thread_` and then `async_dispatch_thread_` without stopping them.
- In `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::~PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient()`, drain the dispatch threads on all local devices, stop `async_work_runner_`, and then call `LocalDeviceState::Destroy()` on all local devices, so that device streams and worker threads are torn down while the `LocalDeviceState` objects (and `host_memory_allocator_`) are still alive.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007464640

display_title: PR #50805: [XLA:GPU] Record scheduler cost estimates in the HLO

head_commit.message:
PR #50805: [XLA:GPU] Record scheduler cost estimates in the HLO

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50805

📝 Summary of Changes

Saves the cost estimates used by the scheduler and their provenance into op metadata of the optimised HLO.
Metadata should not enter any hashes/fingerprints that are required to be stable, but this is initially under a flag to provide an escape hatch in case of bugs.

🎯 Justification

It can be hard to figure out why the scheduler makes decisions; this provides some visibility and makes it easier to evaluate from profiles whether the costs assumed during scheduling were accurate estimates of the final achieved performance.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

n/a

🧪 Unit Tests:

Unit tests added.

🧪 Execution Tests:

n/a
Copybara import of the project:

--
e12ac984e18bec20a59c6c2e4e1ad8df8f12e39f by Olli Lupton <olupton@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Record scheduler cost estimates in HLO

With --xla_gpu_collect_cost_model_stats the latency hiding scheduler records,
for each instruction it schedules, the cost it used and the estimator that
produced it in two new OpMetadata fields, scheduler_cost_us and
scheduler_cost_source.

These estimates are propagated to profiler annotations.

Merging this change closes #50805

display_title: [XLA:SE] Add StreamExecutor::HostMemoryUnregisterMaySynchronize().

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SE] Add StreamExecutor::HostMemoryUnregisterMaySynchronize().

Add `StreamExecutor::HostMemoryUnregisterMaySynchronize()`, which returns true if `HostMemoryUnregister()` may synchronize with work in flight on the executor's device (e.g. kernels or collectives that may in turn wait on other devices). Callers can use this to avoid unregistering host memory concurrently with launches on that device.

`CudaExecutor` returns true since `cuMemHostUnregister` may synchronize with work in flight on the context that owns the registration. Other executors return false by default.

display_title: Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

head_commit.message:
Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` were lowered as large graphs of primitive operations, which made both compilation and execution slow.

This change replaces the CPU implementation of `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` with C++ kernels in a new `_math` extension, vectorized with Highway and parallelized across threads for large arrays. Both kernels keep the same accuracy bounds (`<= 1.0` ULP for `float16`/`float32`/`float64` and `<= 0.5` ULP for `bfloat16`), support sharded execution and `jax.export`, and fix batch partitioning for custom calls when all dimensions are batch dimensions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007250327

head_commit.message:
Let backends ignore the layout constraints of custom calls

Adds LayoutAssignment::IgnoreCustomCallLayoutConstraints. A backend returns
true for a custom call that does not depend on the layouts of its operands
and results. Layout assignment then neither constrains its operands nor
copies its aliased operands, and afterwards sets its
operand_shapes_with_layout to the assigned layouts. The default is false, so
no backend changes behavior.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Place register_extension_info load last in cc_to_llvm_ir.bzl

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Place register_extension_info load last in cc_to_llvm_ir.bzl

#ai-generated

Exporting to OpenXLA replaces the internal `register_extension_info` load with a no-op `def` stub. Placing that load before other `load` statements in `xla/codegen/intrinsic/cpp/cc_to_llvm_ir.bzl` emits a `def` ahead of `load(...)` statements in open source, which fails Bazel Starlark parsing (`load statements must appear before any other statement`).

Move the `register_extension_info` load after all other `load` statements with `# buildifier: disable=out-of-order-load`, matching other exported XLA Starlark files.

head_commit.message:
Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` were lowered as large graphs of primitive operations, which made both compilation and execution slow.

This change replaces the CPU implementation of `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` with C++ kernels in a new `_math` extension, vectorized with Highway and parallelized across threads for large arrays. Both kernels keep the same accuracy bounds (`<= 1.0` ULP for `float16`/`float32`/`float64` and `<= 0.5` ULP for `bfloat16`), support sharded execution and `jax.export`, and fix batch partitioning for custom calls when all dimensions are batch dimensions.

head_commit.message:
`ConstraintPropagator` seeded 16-bit floating-point intervals on every instruction across all computations—clamping intermediate 32-bit reduction accumulators inside fused computations to `[-65504, 65504]`—did not propagate `get-tuple-element` user bounds across tuple-returning fusion boundaries, and only split output bounds across `add` operands when one operand was constant. name: CI
display_title: Skip bazel-diff on global Bazel config skew

head_commit.message:
Skip bazel-diff on global Bazel config skew

In GitHub Actions pull request jobs, `actions/checkout` checks out the synthetic merge commit while `build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` checks out the PR's `merge-base` and branch tip. If `main` updated `.bazelversion`, `.bazelrc`, or `MODULE.bazel` after the PR branched, `bazel-diff` starts a Bazel server with older version or startup flags in the shared `output_base`. When the subsequent test step runs on the merge commit and shuts down that server, containers whose PID 1 does not reap child processes leave a zombie server process and Bazel aborts with exit code 36.

Therefore this change checks whether any global Bazel configuration file differs between `head_sha` and the checked-out `HEAD` before invoking Bazel, and falls back to `Decision=FULL` immediately if so. This avoids starting a mismatched Bazel daemon (and avoids failing `cquery` on flags added on `main`) while keeping warm Skyframe reuse when global Bazel configs match.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008163053

display_title: Sanitize `module_name` in `GetDumpSubdirPath` using `xla::SanitizeFileName` to prevent path traversal

head_commit.message:
Sanitize `module_name` in `GetDumpSubdirPath` using `xla::SanitizeFileName` to prevent path traversal

`pjrt::GetDumpSubdirPath` previously passed `module_name` directly to `xla::FilenameFor` without sanitizing path separators (`/` and `\`). A crafted MLIR module name containing traversal sequences (such as `/../../...` or `../../...`) could inject path separators into the subdirectory name joined onto `dump_to_path`, allowing `RecursivelyCreateDir` and subsequent compilation dumps to escape the intended root dump directory.

This change:
- Sanitizes `module_name` with `xla::SanitizeFileName` before passing it to `xla::FilenameFor`, replacing `/`, `\`, `[`, `]`, and `' '` with `_` so the generated subdirectory name is strictly a single flat path component under `dump_to_path`.
- Adds unit test coverage in `dump_test.cc` verifying `tsl::io::Dirname(dump_subdir) == temp_dir` across multiple path traversal boundary patterns (`ASSERT_OK_AND_ASSIGN`).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Convert <=8-bit integer and F32 dot operands to BF16 by default

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Convert <=8-bit integer and F32 dot operands to BF16 by default

Every <=8-bit integer value (`S1`, `U1`, `S2`, `U2`, `S4`, `U4`, `S8`, `U8`) is
losslessly representable in `BF16` (which has 8 significand bits). Previously,
`DotOperandConverter` upcasted the integer operand of a mixed `(int<=8, f32)`
`dot` to `F32`, forcing the `dot` onto the TF32 Tensor Core path
(`dot(f32, f32) -> f32`) even when `PrecisionConfig` had default precision
(`ALG_UNSET` and `DEFAULT` operand precision).

Update `DotOperandConverter` so that when a `dot` with `F32` or `BF16` output
and default precision multiplies an <=8-bit integer operand by an `F32` operand
on a target that supports fast `BF16` GEMMs (Ampere+ on CUDA, or ROCm GPUs with
`BF16` support excluding MI200) and `tensor_float_32_execution_enabled()` is
true, both operands are converted to `BF16` (`dot(bf16, bf16) -> f32`/`bf16`).
Explicit higher precision requests (`HIGH`, `HIGHEST`, explicit `DotAlgorithm`s,
or disabled TF32 execution) and targets without `BF16` GEMM support continue to
upcast to `F32`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Adds StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator, which returns a
MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die)
of the device. The CUDA implementation creates the physical memory with
cuMemCreate, using location type CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN
(CUDA 13.4 and newer). It rejects out-of-range domain ids, older CUDA
versions, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false), and never falls back to
whole-device memory.

display_title: Fix base branch fetch in clang-format workflow

head_commit.message:
Fix base branch fetch in clang-format workflow

In `.github/workflows/clang_format.yml`, `git fetch origin main --depth=1` truncates `origin/main` to a single commit, so `git merge-base` in `build_tools/ci/run_clang_format.sh` fails as soon as `main` advances past a PR's base commit. Hardcoding `main` also breaks PRs that target release branches.

So this change switches checkout to `fetch-depth: '100'` (avoiding downloading all branches and tags) and fetches the full history of `${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-main}`, matching `.github/workflows/clang_tidy.yml`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Enable `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` by default.

Enabling `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` by default lowers eligible associative `HloOpcode::kScan` ops (`cumsum`, `cumprod`, `cummin`, `cummax`) on GPU to Triton fusions (`__triton`) via `ScanRewriterTriton`.

Across the 35-cell `f32[B, N]` scan benchmark sweep (`B` in `{1, 4, 16, 64, 256}`, `N` in `{1024, 4096, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144}`), the Triton scan emitter achieves 1.45x–3.20x speedups on A100, 1.16x–3.62x on H100, and 1.15x–4.35x on B200 with zero regressions, and fuses `softmax` + exclusive `cumsum` + mask (`K <= 128`) into a single Triton kernel (1.90x–2.19x speedup on H100 and B200).

display_title: [IFRT] Canonicalize names in MLIR fingerprints

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Canonicalize names in MLIR fingerprints

`FingerprintModuleOp` hashes the module name and the symbol names of `sdy.mesh`
ops, so programs that differ only in these names get different fingerprints.
`FingerprintOptions` adds `canonicalize_module_name` and
`canonicalize_sdy_mesh_names`, which a bytecode attribute callback implements by
encoding these names as IDs. Mesh definitions, mesh uses and the order of mesh
names still contribute, and the IR is not mutated. `FingerprintModuleOp` and
`HloProgram::Fingerprint` take the options explicitly; default options keep
existing fingerprints.

display_title: Fix clang-tidy target selection for CUDA sources

head_commit.message:
Fix clang-tidy target selection for CUDA sources

`@bazel_clang_tidy` always appends `-xc++` and forwards target `copts` directly to `clang-tidy`, so running it on `.cu.cc` files or `cuda_library` targets fails on CUDA device syntax and NVCC-only flags (such as `-Xcuda-fatbinary` and `-nvcc_options`).

So this change excludes `.cu.cc` and `.cu.h` files from `CHANGED_FILES` in `build_tools/ci/run_clang_tidy.sh` (letting CUDA-only changes exit before starting Bazel) and filters `cuda_library` and `.cu` targets out of the `cquery` target list when a shared header or `.cc` file changes.

name: CI
display_title: Skip bazel-diff on global Bazel config skew

head_commit.message:
Skip bazel-diff on global Bazel config skew

In GitHub Actions pull request jobs, `actions/checkout` checks out the synthetic merge commit while `build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` checks out the PR's `merge-base` and branch tip. If `main` updated `.bazelversion`, `.bazelrc`, or `MODULE.bazel` after the PR branched, `bazel-diff` starts a Bazel server with older version or startup flags in the shared `output_base`. When the subsequent test step runs on the merge commit and shuts down that server, containers whose PID 1 does not reap child processes leave a zombie server process and Bazel aborts with exit code 36.

Therefore this change checks whether any global Bazel configuration file differs between the checked-out `HEAD` and `diff_base` or `head_sha` before invoking Bazel, and falls back to `Decision=FULL` immediately if so. This avoids starting a mismatched Bazel daemon (and avoids failing `cquery` on flags added on `main`) while keeping warm Skyframe reuse when global Bazel configs match.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008163053

PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

name: CI
display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] SKIP_PROFILED: allocate temp buffers in the VA reservation from the first execution PR 2/2

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] SKIP_PROFILED: allocate temp buffers in the VA reservation from the first execution

- In SKIP_PROFILED, automatically selected preallocated temp buffers are
  allocated at their VA reservation offsets from the first execution, as
  in SKIP_TEMP. A reservation created while profiling lays out every
  profile candidate (VA only); one created after the transition covers
  only the selected set.
- Before, the profiling executions took the temp from the regular VMM pool
  and the transition allocated a second copy in the reservation. The first
  copy stayed behind as stale allocator state, so each temp was held twice.
  On ROCm every peer imports each VMM mapping into its GTT, so the second
  copy overflowed GTT and multi-GPU runs hung; on CUDA it held extra device
  memory.
- Update the SKIP_PROFILED documentation in xla.proto and the class.
- Add unit tests for a reclaim-exempt temp under a one-temp PA budget, a
  shared profiling-phase reservation and a failed profiling execution;
  extend an existing test to the first execution.

name: CI
display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] Release reservation-backed temp buffers when a VA-remapped execution fails before running PR 1/2

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Release reservation-backed temp buffers when a VA-remapped execution fails before running

- GpuExecutable and the PJRT GPU client return without TearDown when
  setup before execution fails. With command buffer VA remapping
  (SKIP_TEMP, and SKIP_PROFILED after its transition) the temp buffer
  stayed active at its reservation address, so every later execution
  failed with ALREADY_EXISTS.
- Teardown now goes through ExecutionScope::TearDown in both callers. The
  VA-remap scope records the temps it allocates in the reservation. Its
  TearDown releases them and keeps the ones whose release fails; its
  destructor releases the ones still recorded.
- ExecutionScope stores the device ordinal it is created for; its methods
  no longer take one.
- Add unit tests for a failed allocation, an execution without teardown,
  a teardown before an early return, and a teardown that fails to release
  one of two temps.

display_title: Add `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` to query the Linux dma-buf

head_commit.message:
Add `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` to query the Linux dma-buf
location (`{fd, offset, size}`) of an on-device buffer for external
access.

The query returns the raw buffer's location within the underlying
dma-buf, with `offset` measured from the dma-buf start. The location
remains valid as long as the caller holds a reference to the raw
buffer, while ordering external access against device execution
remains the caller's responsibility. Unsupported backends and plugins
built against earlier API versions return `Unimplemented`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Preserve shared `inlineable="xla_late"` callees in FlattenCallGraph.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve shared `inlineable="xla_late"` callees in FlattenCallGraph.

* Add `flatten_non_inlineable_calls` option (default `false`) to `FlattenCallGraph`.
* Constrain the single-argument `bool` constructor with `std::enable_if_t<std::is_same_v<T, bool>>` so passing a function pointer (e.g. `AddPass<FlattenCallGraph>(FlattenCallGraph::SkipCloningForCalls)` in compiler pass pipelines) binds to the `absl::AnyInvocable` overload instead of implicitly converting the non-null function pointer to `true` via C++ standard boolean conversion.
* When `flatten_non_inlineable_calls=false`, skip cloning callees at `kCall` sites annotated with `frontend_attributes={inlineable="xla_late"}` so deduplicated computations remain shared across late-inlined call sites until explicit late flattening (`FlattenCallGraph(/*flatten_non_inlineable_calls=*/true)`).
* Handle mixed callers (where both standard calls or while/conditional bodies and `xla_late` calls target the same computation)

name: CI
display_title: Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

head_commit.message:
Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

With `prefer_estimated_configs`, each instruction's estimated configs were
compiled serially on the calling thread.

Now we split the config assignment into 3 stages:
* Look up forced or cached config
* If applicable, get an estimated config <- now they are compiled in parallel
* Get a tuned (if autotuning) or a first compilable/default config (if not)

This is similar to what we've been doing already, just split into stages more explicitly. We need to trigger the tuned and fallback config getter from the main thread, since getting supported configs is not thread-safe.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008143797

display_title: Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

head_commit.message:
Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

Heuristic indices returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` depend on the GPU and cuBLASLt version, so the same index can resolve to a different kernel across devices or library updates.

Therefore this change introduces `CublasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` (along with their proto definitions in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cublas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto` and `xla/stream_executor/gpu/blas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto`) to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` implements `GetBlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `GetMatmulAlgorithm` to extract and reconstruct `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptors, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` and `BlasLt::GetOrCreateMatmulPlanWithAlgorithm` add overloads accepting `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm`.

Therefore this change introduces `CublasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` (along with their proto definitions in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cublas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto` and `xla/stream_executor/gpu/blas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto`) to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` implements `GetBlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `GetMatmulAlgorithm` to extract and reconstruct `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptors, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` and `BlasLt::GetOrCreateMatmulPlanWithAlgorithm` add overloads accepting `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm`.
